title: Parallel Speed-Ups Not As Expected
description:
Hello, 

I'm working on parallelizing across many resamples with a large dataset. I ran into some of the issues described in #376 and #384 , and was glad to see that in Tune 0.2.0 there was a fix (described in #397). I reproduced the example in #397 below, though switched it to a ranger random forest model. 

With 5,000 rows and 10,000 columns also see that with a single non-parallel worker, the usage peaks at ~3.2-3.5 GB and that with a 8 parallel workers each peaks at ~1.2GB-1.5GB (for a total memory usage between 9GB and 10GB). 

However, the decrease in execution time isn't quite as advantageous as I would expect. With 24 resamples and 8 cores, each core should work through 3 iterations of the model fitting. Based on [this post ](https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2020/11/tune-parallel/) it seems difficult to estimate the time savings _a priori_, but I still expected a greater efficiency than going from 752 seconds elapsed to 558 seconds elapsed.

In [Chapter 10 of the Tidymodeling book](https://www.tmwr.org/resampling.html) it says that 

> Parallel processing with the tune package tends to provide linear speed-ups for the first few cores. This means that, with two cores, the computations are twice as fast. Depending on the data and type of model, the linear speedup deteriorates after 4-5 cores. Using more cores will still reduce the time it takes to complete the task; there are just diminishing returns for the additional cores.

>Let’s wrap up with one final note about parallelism. For each of these technologies, the memory requirements multiply for each additional core used. For example, if the current data set is 2 GB in memory and three cores are used, the total memory requirement is 8 GB (2 for each worker process plus the original). Using too many cores might cause the computations (and the computer) to slow considerably.

So I expect at least a 2-fold increase in computation speed, right? Is there something about the 0.2.0 upgrade that would have affected this? Is this typical behavior or am I missing something in my configuration or my understanding?

title: [FR] last_fit() should use your exact penalty value when fitting glmnet model
description:
Hi,

I should start by saying I am aware of the very good reasons why `glmnet::glmnet()` prefers to fit entire regularization paths rather than single lambdas; and also that even if *your* lambda isn't one of the lambdas in the path, you can still get coefficients and predictions at your lambda via interpolation. I think this is more than satisfactory for hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation given that you only need to fit a single `glmnet()` model to test the performance of many penalty values (i.e. submodels) so it is very efficient.

However, I think that `last_fit()` should fit a `glmnet` model that includes your chosen `penalty` value in the regularization path so that you get **exact** coefficients and predictions rather than interpolated ones for this final `penalty` value.

This could be done by passing in a manual sequence of lambdas that includes your chosen lambda squeezed somewhere in the middle. It would probably require `last_fit_workflow()` to add a flag to the `object` indicating this is the "final" fit (e.g. `object$is_last_fit <- TRUE`) rather than a normal fit, and then a little condition handling in the `glmnet` fitting functions in `parsnip`.

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/d063189185d4bc976c044614333d69290c6707a0/R/last_fit.R#L114-L120

What do you think about this proposal?

Relevant: From the `glmnet` documentation: 
> ...the predict function uses linear interpolation to make predictions for values of s (lambda) that do not coincide with those used in the fitting algorithm. While this is often a good approximation, it can sometimes be a bit coarse.

title: tune_grid failed tuning when set plan(multisession)
description:
Hi, I am using [recipeselectors](https://github.com/stevenpawley/recipeselectors) for feature selection
to speed up the process, I tried doFuture, tune_grid worded fine with plan(sequential), but failed when set plan(multisession)
could you help to solve it?
here is an example from https://github.com/stevenpawley/recipeselectors/issues/1

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
#> Warning: 程辑包'workflowsets'是用R版本4.1.3 来建造的
library(recipeselectors)
data(cells, package = "modeldata")
cells <- cells %>% select(-case)
rec <-
    recipe(class ~ ., data = cells) %>%
    step_corr(all_predictors(), threshold = 0.9) %>% 
    step_select_roc(all_predictors(), outcome = "class", top_p = tune())
mod <- logistic_reg(
    penalty = 0.01,
    mixture = 1
) %>%
    set_engine("LiblineaR") %>%
    set_mode("classification")
wflow <- 
    workflow() %>% 
    add_recipe(rec) %>% 
    add_model(mod)
p_info <- 
    wflow %>% 
    extract_parameter_set_dials() %>% 
    update(top_p = top_p(c(1, 30)))
rs <- vfold_cv(cells)
ctrl <- control_grid(extract = identity)

library(doFuture)
registerDoFuture()
plan(sequential)
# use sequential, succeed
rfe_res <-
    mod %>% 
    tune_grid(
        rec,
        resamples = rs,
        grid = 20,
        param_info = p_info,
        control = ctrl
    )

plan(multisession)
# use multisession, failed
rfe_res <-
    mod %>% 
    tune_grid(
        rec,
        resamples = rs,
        grid = 20,
        param_info = p_info,
        control = ctrl
    )
# x Fold01: preprocessor 1/19: Error in `recipes::prep()`:
```

title: tune_bayes: Optimization stopped prematurely; returning current results. (argument is of length zero)
description:
### The problem: 

I have tried to train the model with tune_bayes. Sometimes it runs correctly, but sometimes the tune_bayes process stops with error.

### Code:

```r

set.seed(1)
splits <- initial_split(cv_set, strata = value)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(training(splits), v = 5, strata = value,repeats = 10)
set.seed(NULL)

rmse_res <- metric_set(rmse)

svm_rec <-
  recipe(value ~ ., data = cv_set)

svm_spec <-
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

svm_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_model(svm_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(svm_rec)

svm_param <-
  svm_wflow %>%
  parameters() %>% 
  update(
    cost = cost(c(-6, 6)),
    rbf_sigma = rbf_sigma(c(-4, 0)))


start_grid <-
  svm_param %>%
  grid_regular(levels = 3)

tic <- Sys.time()
registerDoParallel(cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1)

svm_initial <-
  svm_wflow %>%
  tune_grid(resamples = cv_folds, grid = start_grid, metrics = rmse_res)

stopImplicitCluster()
env <- foreach:::.foreachGlobals
rm(list=ls(name=env), pos=env)


collect_metrics(svm_initial)

ctrl <- control_bayes(verbose = TRUE,seed = sample.int(10^5, 1)) 

set.seed(420)
registerDoParallel(cores = parallel::detectCores() - 1)
svm_bo <-
  svm_wflow %>%
  tune_bayes(
    resamples = cv_folds,
    metrics = rmse_res,
    initial = svm_initial, 
    param_info = svm_param, 
    iter = 30,
    control = ctrl
  )
stopImplicitCluster()
set.seed(NULL)
tic - Sys.time()
```

### Output

title: Output results even if computation of some metrics fails
description:
When some of the metrics can't be computed –as in the example below with SVM which can't compute `roc_auc`–, fitting (e.g. `last_fit`) and tuning (e.g. `tune_grid`)  methods say that the whole model fails and output `NULL`. However, predictions and other metrics could be computed anyway. 
Should it be possible to set only the failing metric to `NA` (or something else) and return the other valid outputs?
This is interesting when fitting/tuning workflow sets with `workflow_map` when `metrics` are set for all the models at the same time.

Thanks for your consideration, and thanks for the `tidymodels` framework!

``` r
library(tidymodels)

data(ad_data, package = "modeldata")

set.seed(42)
split <- initial_split(ad_data, strata = Class)
train <- training(split)

rec <- 
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% 
  step_zv(all_nominal_predictors()) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_nominal_predictors())

spec_svm <- svm_linear(mode = "classification")

wkf_svm <- workflow(rec, spec_svm)
```

title: Allow finalize to work on a recipe / workflow so that ID columns can be handled
description:
Hello,

Let's say I am making an xgboost model where all my data is numeric, like in the [tuning](https://www.tmwr.org/tuning.html) chapter of TMwR book. I can use the `finalize` (~~`finalise`~~, oops) function to conveniently set mtry to be a sensible range with:

```r
rf_spec <- 
  rand_forest(mtry = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("ranger", regularization.factor = tune("regularization"))

pca_rec <- 
  recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train) %>% 
  # Select the square-footage predictors and extract their PCA components:
  step_normalize(contains("SF")) %>% 
  # Select the number of components needed to capture 95% of
  # the variance in the predictors. 
  step_pca(contains("SF"), threshold = .95)

updated_param <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_model(rf_spec) %>% 
  add_recipe(pca_rec) %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  finalize(ames_train)
```

This will set the mtry range as [1, 74]. But the problem I am having is when I am using a recipe that introduces ID columns, for example, let's say we made the recipe in that chapter like this (making one variable an ID column):

```r
pca_rec <- 
  recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train) %>% 
  # Select the square-footage predictors and extract their PCA components:
  step_normalize(contains("SF")) %>% 
  # Select the number of components needed to capture 95% of
  # the variance in the predictors. 
  step_pca(contains("SF"), threshold = .95) %>%
  update_role(MS_SubClass, new_role = "ID") # arbitrary choice of ID column
```

I now can't use the code:

```r
updated_param <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_model(rf_spec) %>% 
  add_recipe(pca_rec) %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  finalize(ames_train)
```

Because this will set the mtry range as [1, 74]. But it should be 73. It's not a problem as such as the tuning code will still run, but it just seems a little disjointed to me so currently I would do something like:

```r
updated_param <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_model(rf_spec) %>% 
  add_recipe(pca_rec) %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  update(mtry = mtry(c(1L, pca_rec$var_info %>% filter(role != "ID") %>% nrow())))
```

Is there a better way to do this and/or can finalize be evolved to allow a workflow or recipe to be used as an argument, instead of a tibble, where the function takes into account that some variables are ID columns?

Thanks.

title: Controlling metric event_level for last_fit()
description:
## The problem

Hi,

Maybe I'm missing something, but how does `last_fit.workflow` know which `event_level` to use for metric computations? All other fitting functions allow the user to specify this via `control` argument, but this function defines the controller inside the function itself (see below) via `control_resamples()`. `control_resamples()` has `event_level = 'first'` by default, yet when I use `last_fit()` it returns the metrics for `event_level = 'second'`, which is actually what I want. I am just not sure where `last_fit` is inheriting this behaviour.

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/6897071ff1201e333692db890b87bbc909a46706/R/last_fit.R#L103-L108

## Reprex

``` r
library(tidymodels)

data <- mutate(mtcars, vs = factor(vs))

tt_split <- initial_split(data, prop = 8/10, strata = 'vs')
rs <- bootstraps(training(tt_split), times = 1, strata = 'vs')

wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_model(
    logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>%
      set_engine('glmnet')
  ) %>%
  add_formula(vs ~ .)

results <- tune_grid(
  wflow,
  resamples = rs,
  grid = 1,
  control = control_grid(event_level = 'second')
)

show_best(results, metric = 'roc_auc')
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>    penalty mixture .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config             
#>      <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 0.000227   0.749 roc_auc binary      0.95     1      NA Preprocessor1_Model1

finalize_workflow(
  wflow,
  select_best(results, metric = 'roc_auc')
) %>%
  last_fit(tt_split) %>%
  collect_metrics()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   .metric  .estimator .estimate .config             
#>   <chr>    <chr>          <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 accuracy binary             1 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 2 roc_auc  binary             1 Preprocessor1_Model1
```

title: Nearly flawless code marred by failure to recognize tune_grid
description:
## The problem

I'm using `tidymodels` and associated R packages on the [SMS Spam Collection dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/uciml/sms-spam-collection-dataset) from Kaggle. Specifically, I am using these packages to distinguish "ham" (legit, regular) SMS messages from their spam counterparts. The problem is encountering a non-fatal but highly undesirable error when evaluating performance on the test set. The error message is:

```
Warning message:
No tuning parameters have been detected, performance will be evaluated using the resamples with no tuning. Did you want to [tune()] parameters?
```

The error has persisted despite making sure to adhere to tutorial material read in *Supervised Machine Learning for Text Analysis in R* (chapter 7 specifically) as well as in an [article](https://www.rebeccabarter.com/blog/2020-03-25_machine_learning/) written by one Rebecca Barter. Both sources appear to be in accord. I have also followed the advice in an [answer to the same problem](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64843271/tune-parameters-not-detected-with-tidymodels) on Stack Overflow, namely, running `devtools::install_github('tidymodels/tune')` and trying again. The error still persisted.

Having said all of that, I was at least able to get figures for accuracy and AUC-ROC for the test set. Both are through the roof, over 0.99 each. I am blown away by what the R community has created.

## Reproducible example

Hopefully the way I'm presenting it is viable. What I've done is create a branch of my repository, `tidymodels-bug`, that is "frozen" as it is right now so I can make further changes on `master` if I desire without affecting your response to how things are exactly now. You will find it here:

https://github.com/readyready15728/sms-spam/tree/tidymodels-bug

I believe I've put `set.seed(42)` wherever necessary, although I doubt the RNG is to blame. In lieu of a `README.md`, which I generally like to add when I believe a project is substantially complete, I will give you a brief description here. The original dataset, `sms.csv`, has only ~13% spam, so I wrote a script called `balance.R` to make them about 50/50 in a new file called `sms-balanced.csv`. `learn.R` then takes over, first performing cross validation with the training set, saving the fit to speed things up later (or alternatively loading an existing fit), then evaluating the performance on the test set in a similar fashion, also using the same saving mechanism.

The training set evaluation works fine. It's testing evaluation where the error occurs. I made sure to check both of my sources thoroughly to make sure I was doing things right and I don't think I made an error. I can at least see accuracy and AUC-ROC and they are highly satisfactory, almost perfect even, but I want the full set of metrics specified towards the very beginning without the error.

title: New parsnip model, finalize_workflow error
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with finalize_workflow. I want to add a new model and I have used the example from [issue 203](https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/203).
Everything work until finalize_workflow.
Thanks in advance for your help.

## Reproducible example

```r
## copy your code to the clipboard and run:
reprex::reprex(si = TRUE)
```

```r

library(tidymodels)
set_new_model("gauss_rbf")


set_model_mode(model = "gauss_rbf", mode = "regression")
set_model_engine(
  "gauss_rbf", 
  mode = "regression", 
  eng = "kernlab"
)
set_dependency("gauss_rbf", eng = "kernlab", pkg = "kernlab")

#show_model_info("gauss_rbf")


set_model_arg(model = "gauss_rbf",
              eng = "kernlab",
              parsnip = "rbf_sigma", ## rbf_sigma exists for svm in dials
              original = "rbf_sigma",
              func = list(pkg = "dials", fun = "rbf_sigma"),
              has_submodel = FALSE)
#show_model_info("gauss_rbf")


# Step 2. Create the model function ---------------
gauss_rbf <-
  function(mode = "regression",  rbf_sigma = NULL) {
    # Check for correct mode
    if (mode  != "regression") {
      rlang::abort("`mode` should be 'regression'")
    }
    
    # Capture the arguments in quosures
    #args <- list(sub_classes = rlang::enquo(sub_classes))
    args <- list(rbf_sigma = rlang::enquo(rbf_sigma))
    
    # Save some empty slots for future parts of the specification
    new_model_spec(
      "gauss_rbf",
      args = args,
      eng_args = NULL,
      mode = mode,
      method = NULL,
      engine = NULL
    )
  }

# Step 3. Add a fit module -------------------------
gauss_rbf_wrap <- function(formula, data, rbf_sigma) {
  model <- kernlab::gausspr(x = formula, 
                            data = data, 
                            kpar = list(sigma = rbf_sigma),
                            type = "regression",
                            kernel = "rbfdot")
  return(model)
}
set_fit(model = "gauss_rbf",
        eng = "kernlab",
        mode = "regression",
        value = list(
          interface = "formula",
          protect = c("formula", "data"),
          func = c(fun = "gauss_rbf_wrap"),
          defaults = list()))
# show_model_info("gauss_rbf")

set_encoding(
  model = "gauss_rbf",
  eng = "kernlab",
  mode = "regression",
  options = list(
    predictor_indicators = "traditional",
    compute_intercept = TRUE,
    remove_intercept = TRUE,
    allow_sparse_x = FALSE
  )
)


# Step 4. Add modules for prediction -------------------

set_pred(model = "gauss_rbf", 
         eng   = "kernlab", 
         mode  = "regression", 
         type  = "numeric", 
         value = list(
           pre = NULL, 
           post = function(results, object) as.vector(results) , 
           func = c(pkg = "kernlab", fun = "predict"), # need to register
           # the package, otherwise predict fails
           args = list(
             object = expr(object$fit), 
             newdata = expr(new_data), 
             type = "response")))

#  show_model_info("gauss_rbf")



gauss_model <- gauss_rbf(mode = "regression", rbf_sigma = 0.1) %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

gauss_model %>%
  translate()


# test on data

data(mpg)
mpg <- mpg[, c(3:5, 9)] # select only numeric

split <- initial_split(mpg, 0.8)
training <- training(split)
testing <- testing(split)

gauss_fit <- gauss_model %>%
  fit(formula = hwy ~.,
      data = training)

gauss_fit


predict(gauss_fit,
        testing)


testing %>%
  bind_cols(predict(gauss_fit,
                    testing)) %>%
  metrics(truth = hwy, estimate = .pred)


folds <- vfold_cv(training, 10)

gauss_tune <- gauss_rbf(mode = "regression", rbf_sigma = tune::tune()) %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

gauss_tune


gauss_grid <- grid_regular(rbf_sigma(c(0, 0.5), trans = NULL),
                           levels = 5)

gauss_grid



tune_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(gauss_tune) %>%
  add_formula(hwy ~ .)

tuned_grid <- tune_grid(
  tune_wf,
  folds,
  grid = gauss_grid
)



best_model <- tuned_grid %>% select_best(., "rmse")

# error
finalize_workflow(tune_wf, best_model)


# session info
sessionInfo()
```

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Reduce data transfer overhead when tuning in parallel
description:
**Summary**: it seems all folds of cross validation are sent to every single parallel worker, even when each worker may only use 1 single fold, causing big unnecessary data transfer overhead. I'm new to this, so my understanding of the code could be wrong.

**Details**: In `tune:::tune_grid_loop()`, the potentially parallel `%op%` calls `tune:::tune_grid_loop_iter_safely()` with the full  `resamples` object as an function argument. This seems very odd, as for PSOCK workers, the entire `resamples` object (which is n folds bigger than the training data set) is sent to each and every worker, even though each worker may end up using only 1 of those folds. That's just based on my understanding of how parallel::\`%dopar%\` works but I haven't done any more tests.

Indicative current code from R/grid_code_paths.R `tune_grid_loop()`
```
results <- foreach::foreach(
  iteration = iterations,
  seed = seeds,
  .packages = packages,
  .errorhandling = "pass"
) %op% {
  tune_grid_loop_iter_safely(
    iteration = iteration,
    resamples = resamples,
    grid_info = grid_info,
    workflow = workflow,
    metrics = metrics,
    control = control,
    seed = seed
  )
```

Indicative change:
```
results <- foreach::foreach(
  split = resamples$splits,
  seed = seeds,
  .packages = packages,
  .errorhandling = "pass"
) %op% {
  tune_grid_loop_iter_safely(
    split = split,
    grid_info = grid_info,
    workflow = workflow,
    metrics = metrics,
    control = control,
    seed = seed
  )
```

title: Problematic extra memory usage when tune_grid run in parallel compared to serial
description:
## The problem

I've been using tune_grid() for logistic regression with glmnet with a data set that has many predictors (~50,000). When running tune_grid() without parallelization, the memory usage was within my expectations (~1 GB). However, when I tried running the code with parallelization (doParallel with 20 cores), I found that the memory usage had spiked. Each core was using ~18 GB, and with 20 cores, the total memory usage on the server was near 200 GB. Even with using fewer cores, the memory usage was too much when run in parallel, so I'm now running my script without parallelization to ensure the memory usage isn't a problem.

I'm not much an expert on memory usage in R, and I'm new to tidymodels, so I may be misunderstanding something, but I figured since the non-parallel execution was much smaller on a per-core basis, something was probably going wrong with the parallelization.

I've been able to create a reproducible example with a less extreme data set. Here, with 10,000 predictors, I see the per-core memory usage at ~500 MB, but when run in parallel with 8 cores, the per-core usage increases to 731 MB. This example seems to be replicating what I was seeing with my real data set, but on a smaller scale. You can try increasing the number of predictor variables to see larger discrepancies between serial and parallelized versions.

Any idea what might be going on? Thanks for your help!

## Reproducible example

```r
##### Libraries #####
require( "tidymodels" )
require( "foreach" )
require( "doParallel" )
require( "tictoc" )
require( "glmnet" )
require( "tidyverse" )


set.seed( 4235 )

# Create data set
predictor_names <- str_c( "pred", 1:10000 )
id <- 1:150
data <- expand_grid( id, predictor_names ) %>%
  mutate( value = rnorm( n = n() ) ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = predictor_names, values_from = value ) %>%
  mutate( outcome = as.factor( as.character( rbernoulli( n(), p = 0.3 ) ) ) ) %>%
  select( id, outcome, everything() )

# Set up model training parameters
n_iters <- 8
prop_training <- 0.66
n_fold_hyperparameter <- 3
lambdas_range <- 10^seq( -2, 0, by = 0.5 )


##### Set model type and engine #####
glm_model <- logistic_reg( penalty = tune(), mixture = 0.5 ) %>%
  set_engine( "glmnet" )


##### Set data processing recipe #####
cur_recipe <- recipe( data ) %>%
  # General processing
  update_role( id, new_role = "ID" ) %>%
  
  # Specific outcome/predictor processing
  update_role( outcome, new_role = "outcome" ) %>%
  update_role( starts_with( "pred" ), new_role = "predictor" ) %>%
  step_zv( all_predictors() )


##### Set the workflow #####
cur_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model( glm_model ) %>%
  add_recipe( cur_recipe )


##### Select training and testing data #####
cur_testing_training_splits <- initial_split( data, prop = prop_training, strata = outcome )

# Get testing data
cur_testing_data <- testing( cur_testing_training_splits )

# Get training data
cur_training_data <- training( cur_testing_training_splits )


##### Train the model #####
# Set training grid
cur_training_grid <- tibble( penalty = lambdas_range )

# Set CV
cur_cv_folds <- vfold_cv( cur_training_data, v = n_fold_hyperparameter, repeats = n_iters, strata = outcome )

# Train model on a single core
tic( "Train model without parallelization" )
cur_training_results <- cur_workflow %>%
  tune_grid( resamples = cur_cv_folds,
             grid = cur_training_grid,
             metrics = metric_set( roc_auc, pr_auc, accuracy, npv, ppv, yardstick::sensitivity, yardstick::specificity, yardstick::precision, yardstick::recall ) )
toc()



##### Train the model in parallel #####
# Initialize cores for parallel processing
ncores <- 8
cl <- makeCluster( ncores )
registerDoParallel( cl )

# Train model with parallelization
tic( "Train model with parallelization" )
cur_training_results_parallel <- cur_workflow %>%
  tune_grid( resamples = cur_cv_folds,
             grid = cur_training_grid,
             metrics = metric_set( roc_auc, pr_auc, accuracy, npv, ppv, yardstick::sensitivity, yardstick::specificity, yardstick::precision, yardstick::recall ) )
toc()

# Clean up cores
stopCluster( cl )
```

title: more RNG consistency
description:
First, we should make sure that package dependencies do not [change the RNNG state](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49640909/why-would-an-r-package-load-random-numbers) when they are loaded. For example: 

```
> set.seed(1)
> runif(1)
[1] 0.2655087
> 
> set.seed(1)
> library(forecast)
Registered S3 method overwritten by 'quantmod':
  method            from
  as.zoo.data.frame zoo 
> runif(1)
[1] 0.3721239
```

Second, currently `tune` resets the RNGkind after usage: 

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'tune':
#>   method                   from   
#>   required_pkgs.model_spec parsnip

RNGkind()
#> [1] "Mersenne-Twister" "Inversion"        "Rejection"
```

``` r
set.seed(6735)
folds <- vfold_cv(mtcars, v = 5)
```

``` r
spline_rec <-
  recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) %>%
  step_ns(disp, deg_free = tune("disp")) %>%
  step_ns(wt, deg_free = tune("wt"))

lin_mod <-
  linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")

spline_grid <- expand.grid(disp = 2:5, wt = 2:5)

spline_res <-
  tune_grid(lin_mod, spline_rec, resamples = folds, grid = spline_grid)

RNGkind()
#> [1] "L'Ecuyer-CMRG" "Inversion"     "Rejection"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-06-29 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

We do change the RNG kind (see #331) and [reset it](https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/87a79e4dd01483aa97f02d4d95993360d1421850/R/grid_code_paths.R#L470:L473).  However, it is being reset somewhere so we need to add another `on.exit()`.

title: Helper function to extract fitted workflow from `last_fit()` output
description:
In tidymodels/tidymodels#58, @hfrick pointed out that it is pretty awkward to get out the fitted workflow from the _output_ of `last_fit()`; it's all `$.workflow[[1]]`. 😣 This is what you have to do to get a fitted workflow you can use for prediction.

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'tune':
#>   method                   from   
#>   required_pkgs.model_spec parsnip

set.seed(6735)
car_split <- initial_split(mtcars)

spline_rec <- recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) %>%
  step_ns(disp)

lin_mod <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")

spline_wfl <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(spline_rec) %>%
  add_model(lin_mod)

final_fitted <- last_fit(spline_wfl, car_split)

collect_metrics(final_fitted)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config             
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 rmse    standard       5.74  Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 2 rsq     standard       0.503 Preprocessor1_Model1
collect_predictions(final_fitted)
#> # A tibble: 8 x 5
#>   id               .pred  .row   mpg .config             
#>   <chr>            <dbl> <int> <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1 train/test split 18.1      5  18.7 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 2 train/test split 31.1      9  22.8 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 3 train/test split 16.9     14  15.2 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 4 train/test split 20.4     15  10.4 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 5 train/test split 18.0     16  10.4 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 6 train/test split 28.3     19  30.4 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 7 train/test split  9.04    24  13.3 Preprocessor1_Model1
#> 8 train/test split 23.0     30  19.7 Preprocessor1_Model1


final_fitted$.workflow[[1]]
#> ══ Workflow [trained] ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#> Preprocessor: Recipe
#> Model: linear_reg()
#> 
#> ── Preprocessor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1 Recipe Step
#> 
#> • step_ns()
#> 
#> ── Model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> Call:
#> stats::lm(formula = ..y ~ ., data = data)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)          cyl           hp         drat           wt         qsec  
#>   -19.69774      1.09769     -0.02326     -3.05865     -4.28722      2.80367  
#>          vs           am         gear         carb    disp_ns_1    disp_ns_2  
#>    -3.37155      0.18869      4.33774      0.52292    -12.82725      4.55395
```

<sup>Created on 2021-05-03 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

What do we think about a little helper function to take care of this, like we have the helper functions for the metrics and predictions?  We have `collect_metrics()`, `collect_predictions()` -- maybe `collect_workflow()`? It's nice and parallel from the same structure. I feel like `pull_xx` is another obvious choice but it is getting overloaded quickly for us.

title: tune_grid for workflow does not use parallel backend
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with tune_grid not using the parallel backend from doParallel. I had to make the concrete data a bit bigger to really make sure that it wasn't using the backend, but all of the nodes will just sit unused while the main R for Windows terminal front-end will chug on it. I've run this on two machines and I'll include both session infos just in case

## Reproducible example

``` r
#> Warning: package 'tidyr' was built under R version 4.0.5

data(concrete, package = "modeldata")

###Split Data###

concrete_train <- training(concrete_split)
concrete_test  <- testing(concrete_split)

concrete_folds <- 
  vfold_cv(concrete_train, strata = compressive_strength, repeats = 5)

####Create Recipe###
con_recipe <- 
  recipe(compressive_strength ~ ., data = concrete_train) %>% 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_nzv(all_predictors())  %>% 
  step_interact(~ all_predictors():all_predictors())

#### Specify model & Workflow & Grid###

  linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("glmnet") %>%
  set_mode("regression")
```

title: `fit_resample()` works for KNN, LM, SVM, etc., but not glmnet
description:
```
library(tidyverse)
library(rsample)
library(lubridate)
library(tidymodels)
library(stacks)
library(baguette)

set.seed(1)

df <- data.frame(y  = sample(5000000:120000000, 1000, replace = TRUE),
                 yearr = sample(2015:2021, 1000, replace = TRUE),
                 monthh = sample(1:12, 1000, replace = TRUE),
                 dayy = sample(1:29, 1000, replace = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(weekk = week(ymd(paste(yearr, monthh, dayy))),
         datee = ymd(paste(yearr, monthh, dayy))) |>
  filter(!is.na(datee)) |>
  arrange(-desc(datee))

folds = df |>
  sliding_period(lookback = Inf, # if Inf, then it's chain
                 assess_stop = 2,
                 index = datee,
                 period = 'week',
                 every = 15)

rec_df = recipe(y ~ ., data = df)

metric = metric_set(rmse) # mae, or accuracy and roc_auc for classifications

ctrl_grid = control_stack_grid()
ctrl_res = control_stack_resamples()


# Elastic net
spec_enet =
  linear_reg(mode = 'regression', penalty = 1, mixture = 0.5) |>
  set_engine('glmnet')

rec_enet = rec_df |> # Recipe
  #step_dummy(all_nominal()) |>
  step_zv(all_numeric(), all_outcomes()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric(), -all_outcomes())
#step_zv(all_predictors(), skip = TRUE) |>
#step_normalize(all_numeric(), skip = TRUE)

# add both to a workflow
wf_enet = workflow() |>
  add_model(spec_enet) |>
  add_recipe(rec_enet)

# Tune THIS OR
#resample_enet = fit_resamples(wf_enet,
#                              resamples = folds,
#                              grid = 4,
#                              metrics = metric,
#                              control = ctrl_grid)

# fit to the 5-fold cv OR THIS
resample_enet = fit_resamples(wf_enet,
                              resamples = folds,
                              metrics = metric,
                              control = ctrl_res)
```

Error output for first `resample_enet`:
```
x Slice01: preprocessor 1/1, model 1/1: Error in elnet(xd, is.sparse, ix, jx, y, weights, offset, type.gaussian, : NA/NaN/Inf ...
x Slice02: preprocessor 1/1, model 1/1: Error in elnet(xd, is.sparse, ix, jx, y, weights, offset, type.gaussian, : NA/NaN/Inf ...
x Slice03...
Warning message:
All models failed. See the `.notes` column. 
```

Very similar code is used for KNN, LM, SVM, etc., but it just seems to fail for glmnet. What gives?

title: Unreliable random numbers produced when using doFuture backend
description:
Hi,

I’m using `doFuture` as a `foreach` backend. This is an approximation of the code I’m trying to run:

**Edit:** forgot the doFuture code:
```
library(tidymodels)
library(doFuture)

cores <- parallelly::availableCores()
registerDoFuture()
# Only option available on Macs, as I understand it:
plan("multisession")

data(cells)
set.seed(2369)
tr_te_split <- initial_split(cells %>% select(-case), prop = 3/4)
cell_train <- training(tr_te_split)
cell_test  <- testing(tr_te_split)

set.seed(1697)
folds <- vfold_cv(cell_train, v = 10)

cell_rec <- recipe(
    class ~ .,
    data = cell_train
)

boost_forest_mod <- boost_tree(
    mtry = tune(),
    trees = tune(),
    min_n = tune(),
    learn_rate = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune(),
    loss_reduction = tune(),
    sample_size = tune(),
    stop_iter = tune()
) %>%
    set_engine("xgboost") %>%
    set_mode("classification")

workflow_cells <- workflow() %>%
    add_recipe(cell_rec) %>%
    add_model(boost_forest_mod)

workflow_cells_tuned <- workflow_cells %>%
    tune_grid(
        folds,
        grid = 20,
        metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, precision, recall)
    )
```

title: Example for extracting analysis set
description:
Comment / example extending on #215 .

While we usually care about performance on the holdout set, extracting and comparing performance to the analysis set may sometimes be helpful in determining whether objects exported from a model built on the analysis set are likely to generalize.

I wrote a gist [here](https://gist.github.com/brshallo/516e8e52fb911a96efafbf01d606a113) encoding an example comparing the performance on analysis / assessment as `min_n` changes in a {ranger} random forest model (I wasn't yet aware of the [extract](https://tune.tidymodels.org/reference/extract_recipe.html) funs Max pointed to in #215 ... so could likely be written a bit cleaner):

![](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/c498111162b8f8d4fced8fe07f7b532fe2de3c4a66f68e29b9f29832148ab674/68747470733a2f2f692e696d6775722e636f6d2f316e53687836792e706e67)

I wrote more on this example in the context of prediction intervals [here](https://www.bryanshalloway.com/2021/03/18/intuition-on-uncertainty-of-predictions-introduction-to-prediction-intervals/#cautions-with-overfitting).

title: tune w/ xgboost: `REAL() can only be applied to a 'numeric', not a 'logical'`
description:
## The problem
`tune_grid` completes but all models error. `.notes` all indicate the error: `Error in xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(x, label = y, missing = NA): REAL() can only be applied to a 'numeric', not a 'logical'"`
I've checked the parameters object and am unable to determine where a logical is coming from. I stepped down into the `tune_grid` function and the grid passed into the `foreach` loop checks out, so I'm assuming the model specification for `xgboost` is passing parameters to `xgb.DMatrix` in a way that is causing the error. 
Here are the [data dependencies to run the reprex (19MB)](http://themindful.life/R/reprex.RData).

title: resampled confusion matrix is transposed
description:
With `conf_mat_resamped(tidy = FALSE)`, the matrix is transposed. 

``` r
library(tidymodels)

set.seed(1)
tr <- AppliedPredictiveModeling::easyBoundaryFunc(500, intercept = 6)
te <- AppliedPredictiveModeling::easyBoundaryFunc(500, intercept = 6)

table(tr$class)
#> 
#> Class1 Class2 
#>    450     50
tr$prob <- NULL

set.seed(1)
rs <- vfold_cv(tr)

mod <- rand_forest() %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode("classification")

set.seed(1)
res <-
  mod %>%
  fit_resamples(class ~ .,
                resamples = rs,
                control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE))

mod %>% 
  fit(class ~ ., data = tr) %>% 
  predict(te) %>% 
  bind_cols(te) %>% 
  conf_mat(truth = class, estimate = .pred_class)
#>           Truth
#> Prediction Class1 Class2
#>     Class1    440     17
#>     Class2      6     37

conf_mat_resampled(res)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 3
#>   Prediction Truth   Freq
#>   <fct>      <fct>  <dbl>
#> 1 Class1     Class1  44.5
#> 2 Class1     Class2   1.9
#> 3 Class2     Class1   0.5
#> 4 Class2     Class2   3.1
# Truth in columns, predictions in row
conf_mat_resampled(res, tidy = FALSE)
#>        Class1 Class2
#> Class1   44.5    0.5
#> Class2    1.9    3.1
```

title: Support tuning to a validation dataset (instead of cross-validation)
description:
I was wondering if any consideration has been given to adding an option to the tune functions to use a single validation dataset instead of performing cross-validation. 

Here are my reasons for preferring the use of a validation dataset over cross-validation:

1. My dataset contains several years of customer orders. However, I primarily want the model to fit well on the most recent couple of months of orders. Hence, I use a validation dataset containing the most recent months in order to tune my hyperparameters. (I also use a separate test dataset for final evaluation)

2. I have too many observations & features and not enough computing power to perform cross-validation in a reasonable amount of time.

Thank you!

title: use tunable in tune_args.step
description: `tune_args.step()` has a long white-list. Instead of this, `tunable()` should be run on the step to get the list of arguments that should be evaluated.

title: candidate sets and duplicate parameters
description:
The grid that Bayesian optimization uses to evaluate candidate sets with semi-random but could end up choosing a set of existing parameters, especially if they are integers or qualitative. 

We should do an `anti_join()` on them to filter existing solutions out and exit if there are no additional values to check.

title: acquisition functions
description:
confidence bounds, probability of improvement, etc. 

This should be functions that create a classed object and should have a argument for the metric. These are meant to be passed to the `objective` function.

```r
tunable.step_other <- function(x, ...) {

}
```

title: by can't contain join column id
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with running a simple random forest tuning.

## Reproducible example

```
library(tidymodels)
library(tune)
set.seed(1)

df <- tibble(
  x1 = runif(1000, 5, 10),
  x2 = runif(1000, 20, 30),
  outcome = as.factor(ifelse(x1 + x2 > 32, 1, 0))
)

rec <- recipe(df, outcome ~ .)
rf_mod <- rand_forest(mode = "classification", trees = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("randomForest")
cv_splits <- vfold_cv(df, v = 4)
grid <- expand.grid(trees = c(100, 200))

tune_grid(rec, model = rf_mod, rs = cv_splits, grid = grid)
```

#> `by` can't contain join column `id` which is missing from RHS

title: there should be a method of getting best estimator and best score
description:
As we do tunning like `Bayesian hyper-parameter tuning` or a simple `grid search`, there should be a method to get the best `tuned estimates` e.g.

```r
# define model_spec
spec_xgboost <- boost_tree(mode = "classification", 
                           tree_depth = tune(),
                           trees = tune(),
                           learn_rate = tune(),
                           mtry = tune(),
                           min_n = tune()) %>% set_engine("xgboost")

## The workflow should have a recipe or a formula attached to it.
xgb_wf <- workflow() %>%
            add_model(spec_xgboost) %>%
          add_formula(Class ~ .)

# final grid
grid <- xgb_wf %>%
  param_set() %>%
  update(mtry = mtry(c(1,20)))%>%
  grid_max_entropy(size = 20)

grid_results <- tune_grid(xgb_wf, rs = folds, grid = grid,
                          perf = metric_set(roc_auc),
                          control = grid_control(verbose = TRUE))

get_best_score(grid_results)
get_best_params(grid_results)

tb_results <- tune_Bayes(ames_wflow,rs = cv_splits,initial = initial_grid,perf = metric_set(rmse),
                   objective = exp_improve(foo),
                   iter = 20,
                   control = Bayes_control(verbose = TRUE,uncertain = 10,extract = num_leaves))

get_best_score(tb_results)
get_best_params(tb_results)
```

I called it `get_best_params()` and `get_best_score()`. These set of `best estimate params` should then could be directly passed to the `model fit` to build the `final model`

apologies if its already being implemented. 

Regards,

## The problem

I'm trying out the [ames_mars](https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/master/inst/examples/ames_mars.R) example. I noticed that it gets stuck after 3 `predictions` if I wish to `tune` the `prune_method` argument. In this case I have to kill the RStudio and start again. However, it doesn't get stuck if I don't `tune` the `prune_method` argument.

My other 2 proposals are:

1. Make the `verbose = TRUE` in the `grid_control` or `Bayes_control` as `default` option within `tune_grid` or `tune_bayes` methods because I like to see progress and read whats going on
2. I would like to see `which` arguments of tune are being `fitted` e.g. model 1/1 using the tuning parameters `num_terms = 10, prod_degree = 2` etc.? 

point number 2 happens for `tune_Bayes()` already though:

title: specific tunable methods for some models
description:
* `boost_tree()` for xgboost should map `sample` to `sample_prop()`

* all `glmnet`-related models should modify the `mixture` range to have a lower bound of 0.05

* C5 models should truncate the range of trees to 100

* kknn parameter `dist_power` might need to be truncated to not be near zero

I'm having trouble with tuning xgboost regression models. I've tried to recreate what I'm doing with my real data using Ames housing data below. All models are failing when I use recipe or workflow in the tune_grid but using formula works fine.

``` r
library(tune)
library(AmesHousing)

data_split <- initial_split(ames, strata = "Sale_Price", p = 0.75)

ames_train <- training(data_split)
ames_test  <- testing(data_split)

  recipe(Sale_Price ~ .)

  mtry = tune(),
  trees = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune()
) %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("xgboost")

grid <-
  grid_max_entropy(
    mtry(c(1, 27)),
    trees(),
    min_n(),
    tree_depth(),
    learn_rate(),
    loss_reduction(),
    size = 10,
    original = TRUE
  )

xgb_ctrl <- control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

tuning <- tune_grid(
  recipe,
  model = engine,
  resamples = df_cv,
  grid = grid,
```

```r
boost_tree(mode = "classification") %>%
```

then the user would need to create their own grid. For common engine parameters, there should be something a `tunable.boost_tree()` method that would insert a `dials` reference when someone chooses to optimize `rules`.

title: penalty tune() values
description:
Hi
It appears that when we try to optimize a parameter like penalty if we don't specify the grid it uses some default value. However, certain engines like glmnet provide a more appropriate range for the penalty based on the specific training data. 

It would be helpful in tune() would use the recommended range by the engine if available.

FKG

title: Recommended path from finding best parameters to retraining the model on full training data
description:
I was trying to find such an example in the ```tune``` package documentation, but couldn't find one. It's obviously clear that one could simply pass the best parameters from the tuning process into a new model engine object and just train it on the full data, but it would be handy to have a helper for that. 

It could update the ```workflow()``` with specific, static parameter values that were found in the course of tuning and the user could then ```bind()``` the entire training set to the ```workflow``` OR simply use the ```fit()``` function from ```parsnip``` on such a workflow, in order to fit the final model that could be then used for making predictions. Is something like this already in scope somewhere?

title: switch first arguments to `tune_*()` functions
description:
Right now, the main signatures look like:

```r
tune_grid(formula,  model_sepc...)
tune_grid(recipe, model_sepc, ...)
tune_grid(workflow, ...)
```

but `parsnip::fit.model_spec()` uses:

```
fit(model_spec, formula, ...)
```

To be internally consistent, we should change these to 

```r
tune_grid(model_sepc, formula, ...)
tune_grid(model_sepc, recipe, ...)
tune_grid(workflow, ...)
```

description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with using `tune_grid()` for multiple outcomes that I wish to model. If I have more than one column with an outcome role, I get the same error message as #150.

I'm curious whether there is a better way to do the following:

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(tune)

dta <- tibble::tibble(binary_1  = rbinom(1000, 1, 0.7),
                      binary_2  = rbinom(1000, 1, 0.55),
                      feature_1 = rgamma(1000, 2, 1),
                      feature_2 = rnorm(1000, 10, 20),
                      feature_3 = rpois(1000, 5))

### create a recipe

  recipe(~ .) %>%
  update_role(contains("binary"), new_role = "outcome") %>%
  # Ensure target(s) are factors

ranger_tuner <- rand_forest(trees = tune(), mtry = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode(mode = "classification")

### create a resamples tibble  
bs_resamples <- bootstraps(dta, times = 1)

### fit the gridded models  
fits <- tune_grid(
  ex_recipe,
  model = ranger_tuner,
  resamples  = bs_resamples,
  grid = 10,
  metrics  = metric_set(roc_auc)
```

title: tune_bayes() errors when tuning a recipe plus a finalized model
description:
## The problem

I want to tune parameters of a recipe (e.g., `step_poly(degree = tune())`) and a model simultaneously.
This errors with `tune_bayes()`, when the model has parameters that need to be finalized (e.g., `mtry`) although I used `update()` or `finalize()` beforehand.

All other potential variations of the example below work as expected. For example, it works with `tune_grid()`, it works with `min_n` instead of `mtry`, and it works without the tuning parameter in the recipe.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library("tidymodels")
#> -- Attaching packages -------------------------------------- tidymodels 0.0.3 --
#> v broom     0.5.4     v purrr     0.3.3
#> v dials     0.0.4     v recipes   0.1.9
#> v dplyr     0.8.4     v rsample   0.0.5
#> v ggplot2   3.2.1     v tibble    2.1.3
#> v infer     0.5.1     v yardstick 0.0.5
#> v parsnip   0.0.5

#> x ggplot2::margin()   masks dials::margin()
#> x recipes::step()     masks stats::step()
#> x recipes::yj_trans() masks scales::yj_trans()
library("tune")
library("workflows")

set.seed(2341)

ex_rec <- recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) %>%
  step_poly(disp, degree = tune())

ex_vfold <- vfold_cv(mtcars, 3)

rf_model <-
  rand_forest("regression", mtry = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

rf_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_model) %>%

rf_param <-

rf_param

                        resamples = ex_vfold,

#> Error: Some tuning parameters require finalization but there are recipe parameters
```

title: error tuning model AND recipe
description:
##  The problem

I get the following error when I try to tune a recipe _and_ model:

> Error: Some tuning parameters require finalization but there are recipe parameters that require tuning. Please use parameters() to finalize the parameter ranges.

I originally posted to [RStudio Community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/understanding-tune-update-model-and-parameters/55912?u=ericpgreen) because I was following [an example from the tidymodels workshop deck on tuning](https://conf20-intro-ml.netlify.com/materials/) and figured I was making a mistake. But one of the deck authors [confirmed that she was seeing the same problem](https://community.rstudio.com/t/understanding-tune-update-model-and-parameters/55912/2?u=ericpgreen).

## Reproducible example

Alison made a nice reprex:

```r
library(modeldata)
data("stackoverflow")
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
set.seed(100) # Important!

# make smaller to save time
so_split <- initial_split(sample_n(stackoverflow, size = 300), 
                          strata = Remote)
so_train <- training(so_split)
so_test  <- testing(so_split)
# again, simpler so runs faster
so_folds <- vfold_cv(so_train, v = 2, strata = Remote)

so_rec <- recipe(Remote ~ ., 
                 data = so_train) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) %>% 
  step_lincomb(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_downsample(Remote)

tune_rec <- recipe(Remote ~ ., 
                   data = so_train) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) %>% 
  step_lincomb(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_downsample(Remote, under_ratio = tune())

# no tuning
rf_spec <- 
  rand_forest() %>% 
  set_engine("ranger") %>% 
  set_mode("classification")

# add tuning
tune_spec <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(),
              min_n = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("ranger") %>% 
  set_mode("classification")

# define 3 workflows
tuneboth_wf <-
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(tune_rec) %>% 
  add_model(tune_spec)

tunerec_wf <-
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(tune_rec) %>% 
  add_model(rf_spec)

tunemod_wf <-
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(so_rec) %>% 
  add_model(tune_spec)

# this won't work
tuneboth_wf %>% 
  tune_grid(resamples = so_folds)

# works
tunerec_wf %>% 
  tune_grid(resamples = so_folds)

# works
tunemod_wf %>% 
  tune_grid(resamples = so_folds)
```

title: When fit_resamples/tune_grid is given a prepared recipe, it uses the recipe's template data to fit the model
description:
## The problem

When `fit_resamples()` is called with a prepared recipe, it appears to use the template data associated with the recipe to fit the model and to calculate the predictions + out of sample metrics. This can lead to very misleading performance, especially if the recipe was templated on the full training data (in which case it is reporting **in-sample performance** while claiming to provide out-of-sample).

I show this below, where an overfit model on mtcars has mediocre performance when cross-validated, but a dummy recipe on the full `mtcars` data causes it to have much better performance, and a recipe on a small subset of the data causes it to have terrible performance. This suggests that `fit_resamples` is effectively ignoring the resamples. While I don't show it in the reproducible example below, the same issue also occurs with`tune_grid()` (and perhaps with `tune_bayes()` functions, though I haven't tested it).

This works fine if the recipe is not run through `prep()` first. But I think it's a dangerous behavior that if someone forgets to remove the `prep()`, they will get in-sample error when they're expecting out-of-sample.

If `fit_resamples`, `tune_grid`, or `tune_bayes` are given a prepared recipe, perhaps it should either "un-prep" the recipe, or raise some error (e.g. `fit_resamples() should be run with an un-prepared recipe`)?

## Reproducible example

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(recipes))
library(parsnip)
library(rsample)
#> Loading required package: tidyr
library(tune)

set.seed(2020)

# Predict miles per gallon
folds <- mtcars %>%
  vfold_cv(2)

# Heavily overfit model on mtcars
rf_spec <- rand_forest("regression", trees = 10000, mtry = 5) %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

form <- mpg ~ am + wt + disp + hp + qsec

# As expected, mediocre performance
fit_resamples(form, model = rf_spec, folds) %>%
  collect_metrics()
#> # A tibble: 2 x 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   3.12      2  0.335 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.768     2  0.0628

# Given a dummy recipe that doesn't change anything,
# it suddenly becomes much better
rec <- recipe(form, data = mtcars) %>%
  step_mutate(disp = disp) %>%
  prep()

fit_resamples(rec, model = rf_spec, folds) %>%
  collect_metrics()
```

title: recipes pckage not loaded when running tune_grid in parallel
description:
## The problem

The recipes package is not automatically loaded in the parallel workers, even if `grid_tune` is used with a recipe. The workers are not able to detect recipes' selector functions (`all_predictors()`, `all_numeric()`, etc.) and throw an error.

## Reproducible example

``` r



library(recipes)
library(rsample)
library(parsnip)
library(tune)
library(doParallel)

# Set up parallel processing
all_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)
cl <- makePSOCKcluster(all_cores)
registerDoParallel(cl)

# Example from the `basic grid search` vignette
library(mlbench)
data(Ionosphere)
Ionosphere <- Ionosphere %>% select(-V2)

svm_mod <-
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

iono_rec <-
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = Ionosphere)  %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_dummy(V1)

set.seed(4943)
iono_rs <- bootstraps(Ionosphere, times = 5)

set.seed(35)
grid_rec <-
  tune_grid(
    iono_rec,
    model = svm_mod,
    resamples = iono_rs,
    control = control_grid(allow_par = TRUE)
  )
#> Warning message:
#> All models failed in tune_grid(). See the `.notes` column. 
grid_rec$.notes[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 1 x 1
#>   .notes                                                     
#>  <chr>                                                      
#> 1 "recipe: Error: could not find function \"all_predictors\""
```

## Workaround

A workaround is possible by explicitely using `recipes::` for all selectors. (Note: It isn't even necessary to flag the package in `control_grid(pkgs = "recipes")`).

```r
# Explicitely define the namespace for the selector in the above code
iono_rec <-
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = Ionosphere)  %>%
  step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) %>% 
  step_dummy(V1)
```

This seems somewhat tedious and I believe it should be possible to fully load the recipe package in each worker automatically without unwanted side effects.

title: average predictions
description:
`collect_predictions()` needs an `average` argument that will return one prediction per sample (in cases of bootstrap and repeated CV).  

This should work for all types of predictions. For probabilities, the columns should be averaged and the  set of probability columns should sum to one. ~For classes, the mode should be used.~ (see below)

title: write a developer's guide to tune
description: Describe S3 methods (e.g. `tunable`) and other aspects of working across `dials`, `parsnip`, `recipes`, and `tune`.

title: Tune Aggregation Function?
description: In [this issue](https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/issues/20#issuecomment-449875002) in textrecipes, @kanishkamisra pointed out that the aggregation function used for word embeddings can have a big impact on the model (see also [the paper he mentioned](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.00570)). Would it (conceptually) make sense to make the "aggregation" argument in this new step tunable? I can definitely imagine wanting to tune this, but I'm not sure if that fits within {tune}, or should be handled more manually as a special case.

title: mutate() error when running tune_grid()

I'm running into a `mutate()` error when I try running `tune_grid()`. I can't get the whole error message to display, but when I view the `.notes` column, this is what I see: 

> model 10/50: Error: `mutate()` argument `..object` errored.\n\u001b[34mℹ\u001b[39m `..object` is `purrr::map(1:nrow(y),….

I have never seen this error message before but I did download the latest version of `tune` this morning before attempting to build a model, so I wasn't sure if that had something to do with it. 

I would appreciate any guidance or clarification you can provide as to what I might have done incorrectly.

title: Error when trying to use a custom recipe step when running grid_tune in parallel
description:
I thought I already submitted this issue.  But can't see it.  So I am re-submitting it.

## The problem

When I try running a recipe through a tuning grid that includes a custom step, then it runs perfectly when run in sequential mode, ie when *control_grid(allow_par = FALSE)* is set.  However, trying to run it in parallel causes the following error :
* "recipe: Error in UseMethod(\"prep\"): no applicable method for 'prep' applied to an object of class \"c('step_percentile', 'step')\""

I have used the example code for creating a custom step from the *recipes* package and the example code from the *tune* package to run the tuning grid, with a few modifications that are noted in the code.  The output is quite long,  but only really the last 20 or so lines are significant, as that is where it tries to use the custom step in the tuning grid and produces the error.

I have also tried added the custom step to a package and added *pkgs = "MyPackage"* to the *control_grid(..)*, but it still has the same error.

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> -- Attaching packages ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ tidymodels 0.1.0 --
#> v broom     0.5.5      v recipes   0.1.10
#> v dials     0.0.5      v rsample   0.0.6 
#> v dplyr     0.8.5      v tibble    3.0.0 
#> v ggplot2   3.3.0      v tune      0.0.1 
#> v infer     0.5.1      v workflows 0.1.1 
#> v parsnip   0.0.5      v yardstick 0.0.6 
#> v purrr     0.3.3
#> -- Conflicts --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- tidymodels_conflicts() --
#> x purrr::discard()  masks scales::discard()
#> x dplyr::filter()   masks stats::filter()
#> x dplyr::lag()      masks stats::lag()
#> x ggplot2::margin() masks dials::margin()
#> x recipes::step()   masks stats::step()
library(mlbench)
library(doParallel)
#> Loading required package: foreach
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'foreach'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:purrr':
#> 
#>     accumulate, when
#> Loading required package: iterators
#> Loading required package: parallel

### RECIPES

step_percentile <- function(
  recipe, ...,
  role = NA,
  trained = FALSE,
  ref_dist = NULL,
  approx = FALSE,
  options = list(probs = (0:100)/100, names = TRUE),
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("percentile")
) {

  ## The variable selectors are not immediately evaluated by using
  ##  the `quos` function in `rlang`. `ellipse_check` captures the
  ##  values and also checks to make sure that they are not empty.
  terms <- recipes::ellipse_check(...)

  recipes::add_step(
    recipe,
    step_percentile_new(
      terms = terms,
      trained = trained,
      role = role,
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  )
}

step_percentile_new <-
  function(terms, role, trained, ref_dist, approx, options, skip, id) {
    step(
      subclass = "percentile",
      terms = terms,
      role = role,
      trained = trained,
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  }

get_pctl <- function(x, args) {
  args$x <- x
  do.call("quantile", args)
}

prep.step_percentile <- function(x, training, info = NULL, ...) {
  col_names <- recipes::terms_select(terms = x$terms, info = info)
  ## You can add error trapping for non-numeric data here and so on. See the
  ## `check_type` function to do this for basic types.

  ## We'll use the names later so
  if (x$options$names == FALSE)
    rlang::abort("`names` should be set to TRUE")

  if (!x$approx) {
    ref_dist <- training[, col_names]
  } else {
    ref_dist <- purrr::map(training[, col_names],  get_pctl, args = x$options)
  }

  ## Use the constructor function to return the updated object.
  ## Note that `trained` is set to TRUE

  step_percentile_new(
    terms = x$terms,
    trained = TRUE,
    role = x$role,
    ref_dist = ref_dist,
    approx = x$approx,
    options = x$options,
    skip = x$skip,
    id = x$id
  )
}

## Two helper functions
pctl_by_mean <- function(x, ref) mean(ref <= x)

pctl_by_approx <- function(x, ref) {
  ## go from 1 column tibble to vector
  x <- getElement(x, names(x))
  ## get the percentiles values from the names (e.g. "10%")
  p_grid <- as.numeric(gsub("%$", "", names(ref)))
  approx(x = ref, y = p_grid, xout = x)$y/100
}

bake.step_percentile <- function(object, new_data, ...) {
  require(tibble)
  ## For illustration (and not speed), we will loop through the affected variables
  ## and do the computations
  vars <- names(object$ref_dist)

  for (i in vars) {
    if (!object$approx) {
      ## We can use `apply` since tibbles do not drop dimensions:
      new_data[, i] <- apply(new_data[, i], 1, pctl_by_mean,
                             ref = object$ref_dist[, i])
    } else
      new_data[, i] <- pctl_by_approx(new_data[, i], object$ref_dist[[i]])
  }
  ## Always convert to tibbles on the way out
  as_tibble(new_data)
}

Ionosphere <- Ionosphere %>% select(-V2)

svm_mod <-
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

iono_rec <-
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = Ionosphere)  %>%
  # In case V1 is has a single value sampled
  step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) %>%
  # convert it to a dummy variable
  step_dummy(V1) %>%
  # Scale it the same as the others
  step_range(matches("V1_")) %>%
  step_percentile(recipes::all_numeric()) # The custom step has been added

set.seed(4943)

roc_vals <- metric_set(roc_auc)

cluster = makeCluster(detectCores()) # Create a cluster

    iono_rec,
```

title: New parsnip model can fit and predict, but not tune (tune_bayes and tune_grid)
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with using tune_bayes and tune_grid with a created parsnip model. For the parsnip model, I followed the steps from: https://tidymodels.github.io/parsnip/articles/articles/Scratch.html, where possible, I've recreated the steps from this model (steps 1 - 5a). 

In the below reprex example, step 5c is most relevant to the tune package. 

I've searched for help / previously solved issues and not found much, potentially some examples with created models used with tune_bayes or tune_grid could be helpful (depending on the issue, of course). 

Apologies if the issues are due to my own error/s and thank you in advance for your help :)


## Reproducible example
``` r
############### Adding gausspr as a Parsnip Model
## Load Packages
library(kernlab)
library(tidyverse)
library(parsnip)
library(yardstick)
#> For binary classification, the first factor level is assumed to be the event.
#> Set the global option `yardstick.event_first` to `FALSE` to change this.

#>

#> Loading required package: scales
#>

#> The following object is masked from 'package:purrr':
#>

#> The following object is masked from 'package:readr':
#>

#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dials'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:ggplot2':
#>

# Was unable to figure out how to pass rbf_sigma into the list "kpar", when
# creating the parsnip model, so wrapped the function as below
gauss_rbf_wrap <- function(formula, data, rbf_sigma) {
  model <- kernlab::gausspr(x = formula, 
                            data = data, 
                            kpar = list(sigma = rbf_sigma),
                            type = "regression",
                            kernel = "rbfdot")
  return(model)
}


######## Step 1. Register the Model, Modes, and Arguments
set_new_model("gauss_rbf")

set_model_mode(model = "gauss_rbf", mode = "regression")

set_model_engine("gauss_rbf", 
                 mode = "regression", 
                 eng = "kernlab")

set_model_arg(model = "gauss_rbf",
              eng = "kernlab",
              parsnip = "rbf_sigma", ## rbf_sigma exists for svm
              original = "rbf_sigma",
              func = list(fun = "gauss_rbf_wrap"),
              has_submodel = FALSE)


######## Step 2. Create the model function
gauss_rbf <- function(mode = "regression", rbf_sigma = NULL) {
  # Check for correct mode
  if (mode != "regression") {
    stop("`mode` should be 'regression'", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Capture the arguments in quosures
  args <- list(rbf_sigma = rlang::enquo(rbf_sigma))
  # Save some empty slots for future parts of the specification
  out <- list(args = args, 
              eng_args = NULL,
              mode = "regression", 
              method = NULL, 
              engine = NULL)
  # set classes in the correct order
  class(out) <- make_classes("gauss_rbf") # this doesn't appear as the 
  # class after the fit though?
  out
}


######## Step 3. Add a Fit Module
set_fit(model = "gauss_rbf",
        eng = "kernlab",
        mode = "regression",
        value = list(
          interface = "formula",
          protect = c("formula", "data"),
          func = c(fun = "gauss_rbf_wrap"),
          defaults = list()))


######## Step 4. Add Modules for Prediction
set_pred(model = "gauss_rbf", 
         eng   = "kernlab", 
         mode  = "regression", 
         type  = "numeric", 
         value = list(
           pre = NULL, 
           post = NULL, 
           func = c(pkg = "kernlab", fun = "predict"), # need to register
           # the package, otherwise predict fails
           args = list(
             object = expr(object$fit), 
             newdata = expr(new_data), 
             type = "response")))


######## Step 5. Testing
#### a) Translation
show_model_info("gauss_rbf")

#>  modes: unknown, regression 
#> 
#>  engines: 
#>    regression: kernlab
#>

#>

#>    regression kernlab numeric

gauss_model <- gauss_rbf(mode = "regression", rbf_sigma = 0.1) %>%

gauss_model %>%

# Import data and split
data(mpg)
mpg <- mpg[, c(3:5, 9)] # select only numeric

split <- initial_split(mpg, 0.8)

# The below two functions are where my issues arise
gauss_bayes_results <- tune_bayes(
  object = gauss_tune,

#> Error in .f(.x[[i]], ...): Error when calling gauss_rbf_wrap(): Error in kernlab::gausspr(x = formula, data = data, kpar = list(sigma = rbf_sigma),  :

gauss_grid_results <- tune_grid(
  object = gauss_tune,
  preprocessor = hwy ~.,
  resamples = folds,
```

title: Feature Request:  Is there any investigation into creating a "hypertune space" for the hypertune parameters from random or grid hypertunes
description: I imagine there are papers that explore this, I just don't know about them.  It would seem evident that the reason for using random grids, wouldn't be because it would find the best parameter set, but rather that it would be the best for creating a model to estimate the best hyper-parameters and create a hypertune space to estimate the performance of different combinations of parameters. Is there much research on this and best practices?  I'm currently using kknn after giving up on cv.glmnet.

title: Feature Request: Could the valuereturned from parameters(..) include dummy functions for all .$object[[..]]$trans$transform and $inverse for all parameters
description:
Would it be possible to create dummy *transform* and *inverse* functions for all the parameters returned by a call to parameters(recipe/model/workflow).  These would just be *function(x) x* for non integers and *function(x) as.integer(x)* for integer parameters.

This would make it easier to visualize and work with multiple hyper-parameters as they should be fairly linear if the transform (or dummy non-transform) can be easily applied.

title: Issue with tune_grid giving different results with a simple recipe versus formula

```r
  mutate(year = as.POSIXlt(date)$year + 1900) %>%
```

title: Performance declines when using tune_grid for nested cross validation
description:
## The problem

Hi, I'm trying out different implementations of nested cross-validation. I've coded one that was adapted from the Nested Resampling [article](https://tidymodels.github.io/rsample/articles/Applications/Nested_Resampling.html) in the {rsample} package and one that uses `tune_grid` from the {tune} package. I've noticed significant differences in the performances of each. 

After reading the Optimizations and Parallel Processing [article](https://tidymodels.github.io/tune/articles/extras/optimizations.html#fn1), I thought it might have something to do with whether the parallelization happens in the folds or the resamples, but I'm pretty sure both parallelize in the resamples. From what I can tell, the difference in performance is related to using parsnip to encode the models and something that's happening in tune_grid. When running the tune_grid method for the rf, this message repeats, "i Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry." So maybe there's something extra happening here.

For 100 observations and rf and svm algorithms with 202x2 and 11x1 hyperparameter grids respectively, the complete nested-cv process for the tune_grid implementation (method 1) took 5.27 hrs while using the other way (method 2) took 3.66 hrs. I used 5 repeats of 10 folds for the outer loop and 25 resamples in each fold for the parameter-tuning, inner-loop.  I'm using a 4 core, 16G RAM WIndows 10 machine.

The code I've included only runs 2 folds of the inner-loop. The rest of the code doesn't seem to be very expensive, but if you want, I can include it this thread or in some gists.
Here are some of times:

* Using tune_grid (method 1)
      + parsnip:ranger:::rf = 657.17 sec elapsed (11 min)
      + parsnip::kernlab::svm = 37.36 sec elapsed sec elapsed
 
* Method 2
      + parsnip::ranger::rf = 571.75 sec elapsed (9.5 min)
      + kernlab::svm = 3.46 sec elapsed
      + parsnip::kernlab::svm = 33.44 sec elapsed
 
(aside: Method 2 times had some variance and ranged from around 462 sec to 656 sec depending on if I ran the code directly after method 1 or not.)

I wondering if this is something in my code or some option I'm not including or if this just a gradual accumulation from grid searching 1250 models. I'd appreciate any help you might offer. Thank you.


## Reproducible example

``` r
#####################################
# Set-up
#####################################


pacman::p_load(doFuture, dplyr, purrr, tidymodels, tune)

set.seed(2019)

registerDoFuture()
plan(multiprocess)

# simulated data; generates 10 multi-patterned, numeric predictors plus outcome variable
sim_data <- function(n) {
      tmp <- mlbench::mlbench.friedman1(n, sd=1)
      tmp <- cbind(tmp$x, tmp$y)
      tmp <- as.data.frame(tmp)
      names(tmp)[ncol(tmp)] <- "y"
      tmp
}

# Use small data to tune and compare models
small_dat <- sim_data(100)

ncv_dat <- nested_cv(small_dat, 
                     outside = vfold_cv(repeats = 5), 
                     inside = bootstraps(times = 25)) %>% 
      slice(1:2)




######################################
# method 1: Using Tune pkg 
######################################


error_funs <- metric_set(mae)

rf_params <- crossing("mtry" = c(3,4), "trees" = seq(200, 300))

rf_inner <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = tune()) %>%
      set_engine("ranger", importance = 'impurity') %>%
      set_mode("regression")

svm_params <- tibble(cost = 2 ^ seq(-2, 8, by = 1))

svm_inner <- svm_rbf(cost = tune()) %>%
      set_engine("kernlab") %>%
      set_mode("regression")


tictoc::tic()
tuning_results <- map(ncv_dat$inner_resamples, function(dat, mod_inner, params) {
      tune_grid(y ~ .,
                model = mod_inner,
                resamples = dat,
                grid = params,
                metrics = error_funs)
},
rf_inner, rf_params)
#> i Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry
#> i Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry
tictoc::toc()
#> 667.56 sec elapsed


tictoc::tic()
tuning_results <- map(ncv_dat$inner_resamples, function(dat, mod_inner, params) {
      tune_grid(y ~ .,
                model = mod_inner,
                resamples = dat,
                grid = params,
                metrics = error_funs)
},
svm_inner, svm_params)
tictoc::toc()
#> 40.18 sec elapsed




############################################
# method 2: Adapted from "Nested Resampling"
############################################


error_FUN <- function(y_obs, y_hat){
      y_obs <- unlist(y_obs)
      y_hat <- unlist(y_hat)
      Metrics::mae(y_obs, y_hat)
}

rf_FUN <- function(params, analysis_set) {
      mtry <- params$mtry[[1]]
      trees <- params$trees[[1]]
      model <- parsnip::rand_forest(mode = "regression", mtry = mtry, trees = trees) %>%
            parsnip::set_engine("ranger", importance = 'impurity') %>%
            generics::fit(y ~ ., data = analysis_set)
      model
}

params_list <- list(rf = rf_params)
mod_FUN_list <- list(rf = rf_FUN)


# svm_FUN <- function(params, analysis_set) {
#       cost <- params$cost[[1]]

# inputs params, model, and resample, calls model and error functions, outputs error
mod_error <- function(params, mod_FUN, dat) {
      y_col <- ncol(dat$data)
      y_obs <- assessment(dat)[y_col]
      mod <- mod_FUN(params, analysis(dat))
      pred <- predict(mod, assessment(dat))      
      error <- error_FUN(y_obs, pred)
      error
}

# inputs resample, loops hyperparam grid values to model/error function, collects error value for hyperparam combo
tune_over_params <- function(dat, mod_FUN, params) {
      params$error <- map_dbl(1:nrow(params), function(row) {
            params <- params[row,]
            mod_error(params, mod_FUN, dat)
      })
      params
}

# inputs and sends fold's resamples to tuning function, collects and averages fold's error for each hyperparameter combo
summarize_tune_results <- function(dat, mod_FUN, params) {
      # Return row-bound tibble that has the 25 bootstrap results
      param_names <- names(params)
      furrr::future_map_dfr(dat$splits, tune_over_params, mod_FUN, params) %>%
            # For each value of the tuning parameter, compute the
            # average <error> which is the inner bootstrap estimate.
            group_by_at(vars(param_names)) %>%
            summarize(mean_error = mean(error, na.rm = TRUE),
                      n = length(error))
}
```

title: Error when a custom parsnip model is run in parallel in a tuning grid
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with using a custom parsnip model in a tuning grid when it is run sequentially and is not part of a library, or if it is run in parallel whether part of a library of not.  In both cases the error message is the same

* internal: Error in pkg_list[[1]]: subscript out of bounds

The toy model works correctly, as does the model when it is fitted via parsnip.  
In order to get it to run sequentially I have put the toy model into a package and reference that package.  Otherwise if it  just in the global environment it will fail.  In the example below I have added the toy model to a package so it is not completely reproducible, without doing the same thing.  However, the example below will work if allow_par is set to FALSE.
