title: Having errors when using the tune_grid function in a tidymodels workflow to tune lasso model for binary outcome prediction
description:
## The problem
I am trying to construct a lasso model to predict a binary outcome (`am`). `tidymodels` package is applied through the whole workflow to implement. 

Everything works well when I use single regularization parameter, but until running the `tune_grid` function to tune the lasso model through grid search. According to the error messages, I think  the error is raised due to something incorrect with the class setting with outcome variable(`am`). I have tried to set `type` to `class` / `raw` by adding argument `type = "class"` / `type = "raw"` in the `set_engine()` function. However the error message continued with something like: `# the argument matches multiple formal arguments`.

Is there any remedy to cope with this issue? Thank you for helping.

title: `recipes::step_lag()` and `recipes::step_naomit()` with `fit_resamples()`
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with a running `fit_samples()` (and `tune_grid()` after using `step_lag()`. I tried debugging the issue, and it seemed it had to do with `orig_rows` in `tune:::predict_model_no_grid()` not respecting the fact that there are missing values after the step to create a lag, even when including `recipes::step_naomit()`.

To be honest, I'm not sure what the fix would be for this (assuming that this is a real issue and not just a user error :smile:). I think I understand that `orig_rows` is just trying to keep track of the row number of the rows from the original data set so that it can bind these numbers back to the y values .

## Reproducible example

Copy your code to the clipboard and run:

``` r

library(tidymodels)
library(tune)

data <- 
  mtcars %>% 
  as_tibble()

fmla_rec <- formula(mpg ~ .)

rec_rf <-
  data %>% 
  recipes::recipe(fmla_rec, data = .) %>% 
  recipes::step_lag(recipes::all_numeric(), lag = 1) %>% 
  recipes::step_naomit(recipes::all_predictors())
rec_rf
```

title: when there are notes, print out a few unique examples
description:
This would be in the print methods for `tune_grid()`, `tune_bayes()`, `fit_resamples()` and `last_fit()`. 

Most notes are printed during execution but this would be good if the object is loaded later. 

Here are two examples to test with:

``` r

ames <- make_ames()

# Make sure that you get the same random numbers
set.seed(4595)
data_split <- initial_split(ames, strata = "Sale_Price")

ames_train <- training(data_split)

set.seed(2453)
cv_splits <- vfold_cv(ames_train, v = 10, strata = "Sale_Price")
```

``` r

ames_rec <-
  recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train) %>%
  step_log(Sale_Price, base = 10) %>%
  step_YeoJohnson(Lot_Area, Gr_Liv_Area) %>%
  step_other(Neighborhood, threshold = .1)  %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal()) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors())

svm_model <-
  svm_rbf(
    mode = "classification", cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")


ames_wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(ames_rec) %>%
  add_model(svm_model)

set.seed(4567367)
ames_set <-
  parameters(ames_wflow)

ames_grid <-
  ames_set %>%
  grid_max_entropy(size = 3)

initial_grid <- tune_grid(ames_wflow, resamples = cv_splits, grid = ames_grid)
```

``` r
  step_bs(disp, degree = tune(), deg_free = tune()) %>%

  grid_regular(levels = c(3, 2, 3, 2))
```

title: `fit_resamples` errors with recipes containing filtering steps.
description:
# Issue

The `fit_resamples` function does not play nicely with `step_filter`. Specifically, if one attempts to apply `fit_resamples` to with a recipe that filters rows, the result will throw the standard `mutate` error that occurs when one column is the wrong length, viz., ``Column `.rows` must have length [LENGTH_OF_FILTERED_SPLIT] (the number of rows) or one, not [LENGTH_OF_SPLIT_BEFORE_FILTERING].`` The reason seems to be that in the call to `predict_model`, the `orig_rows` variable is drawn from the original split; however, the number of rows of the output of `predict` reflects the filtering. The relevant lines of code are
https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/e3189ec07e45bb5748c0c3908905f8e834419cc2/R/resample.R#L401
and
https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/e3189ec07e45bb5748c0c3908905f8e834419cc2/R/resample.R#L410-L411

## Reproducible example

The issue can easily be reproduced as follows:

``` r

#>   as.zoo.xts zoo

#> ✖ dplyr::lag()      masks stats::lag()
#> ✖ ggplot2::margin() masks dials::margin()
#> ✖ recipes::step()   masks stats::step()

set.seed(0)

model <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")

recipe <- recipe(cyl ~ ., data = mtcars) %>%
  step_filter(gear != 5)

folds <- vfold_cv(mtcars)

fit_resamples(model, recipe, folds)
```

title: Error while using tune_grid ($ operator is invalid for atomic vectors)
description:
Hi Folks! 
I'm running into trouble with the tuning parameters using the `tune_grid` function while using `tune()` to set hyperparameters in {parsnip}.   

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(yardstick))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tune))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rsample))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(recipes))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(parsnip))


### Create random data  


dta <- tibble::tibble(binary = rbinom(1000, 1, 0.7),
                      feature_1 = rgamma(1000, 2, 1),
                      feature_2 = rnorm(1000, 10, 20),
                      feature_3 = rpois(1000, 5))


### create a recipe  
recipe_df <- dta %>%
  recipe(binary ~ .) %>%
  step_center(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_scale(all_predictors())


### set the engine  
engine <- boost_tree(
  mode = "classification",
  trees = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune()
 
  ) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("xgboost")  


### create a resamples tibble  
df_resamples <- vfold_cv(dta, v = 5)  


### grid of hyperparameters to tune  
grid <-  expand.grid(
  trees = c(50),
  min_n = c(3, 5, 7),
  tree_depth = 100,
  learn_rate = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)
)


### fit te model  
fits <- tune_grid(
```

title: How to collect the metrics for the analysis datasets?
description:
Looking through the documentation, it looks that it not possible to collect easily the metrics for the analysis datasets (cross-validation) after `fit_resamples()`. The `collect_metrics()` is extracting the metrics for the assessment datasets.

Is it feasible to add an `extract_fit()`? Something similar to `extract_model()` or `extract_recipe()`.

title: Conflict between factor indicator names and other columns for tune_grid
description:
# The problem

I'm having trouble running a tuning grid with the formula interface. Here's the reprex:

```r
library(tidymodels)
#> ── Attaching packages ────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels 0.1.0 ──
#> ✔ broom     0.5.6      ✔ recipes   0.1.12
#> ✔ dials     0.0.6      ✔ rsample   0.0.6 
#> ✔ dplyr     0.8.5      ✔ tibble    3.0.1 
#> ✔ ggplot2   3.3.0      ✔ tune      0.1.0 
#> ✔ infer     0.5.1      ✔ workflows 0.1.1 
#> ✔ parsnip   0.1.1      ✔ yardstick 0.0.6 
#> ✔ purrr     0.3.4
#> ── Conflicts ───────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels_conflicts() ──
#> ✖ purrr::discard()  masks scales::discard()
#> ✖ dplyr::filter()   masks stats::filter()
#> ✖ dplyr::lag()      masks stats::lag()
#> ✖ ggplot2::margin() masks dials::margin()
#> ✖ recipes::step()   masks stats::step()
library(mlbench)
data(Ionosphere)
Ionosphere <- Ionosphere %>% select(-V2) %>% mutate(cont = 1:nrow(.)) %>% as_tibble()

resample <- vfold_cv(Ionosphere, v = 2)

svm_mod <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = tune(), min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

params <- finalize(parameters(svm_mod), Ionosphere)
grid_res <- grid_regular(params, levels = 1)

res <- tune::tune_grid(object = svm_mod,
                preprocessor = Class ~ .,
                resamples = resample,
                grid = grid_res
                )
#> i Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry
#> Warning: The `x` argument of `as_tibble.matrix()` must have column names if `.name_repair` is omitted as of tibble 2.0.0.
#> Using compatibility `.name_repair`.
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_warnings()` to see where this warning was generated.
#> x Fold1: model 1/1: Error in predict.ranger.forest(forest, data, predict.all, num...
#> x Fold2: model 1/1: Error in predict.ranger.forest(forest, data, predict.all, num...
#> Warning: All models failed in tune_grid(). See the `.notes` column.
```

I think the problem is coming from due due to `hardhat` converting the column `V1` into an indicator, naming it `V11` and `V10`. This creates a conflict with the actual variables `V10` and `V11`. That is also why we see that warning from `as_tibble.matrix` and repair names. I check to see if this works, and it did:

```r
Ionosphere <- Ionosphere %>% select(-V10, -V11)

resample <- vfold_cv(Ionosphere, v = 2)
res <- tune::tune_grid(object = svm_mod,
                       preprocessor = Class ~ .,
                       resamples = resample,
                       grid = grid_res
                       )
#> i Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry
```

And doesn't have the warning from `as_tibble` either. This is certainly a unique problem which is only present when column names have conflicts. However, perhaps `tune_grid` could be stricter in that sense, checking the column names with the same `as_tibble` call, forcing names to be unique before passing them to the `ranger` call.

title: Feature Request: As an extension to issue #200, could autoplot use the transforms of the hyperparameters
description: Autoplot currently uses the raw values of the hyper-parameters when producing the plot.  Unfortunately this means that hyper-parameters that use log transformations, such as penalty for glmnet, end up all scrunched at about zero, making it fairly unreadable.

title: Feature Request: Implement a Model ID column in the results from `tune_grid()`
description:
Love the `tune_grid()` function. The output wrangling functions `show_best()` and `select_best()` could be enhanced by making it easier to select specific models. 

## Enhancement Request

An enhancement is to include a Model ID and selection interface:

- A Model ID (`.model_id`) column in the results, which enhances the selection process.
- Implement `select_model_id(model_id = "xyz")` to allow the user to quickly select parameters for a Model ID.

## Why Model ID?

It's a good idea to have a unique identifier for parameter combinations. This can make it easier for users to select the model they want to use models other than those with the best mean error metric. Sometimes:

- The best mean error has higher standard error and is therefore has more variability
- Has failed several tuning combinations and is therefore less robust to new data.

## Other Implementations

The `H2O` R package has `h2o::getModel()`, which is very similar to what I'm proposing. It makes it super easy to get specific models with better or worse performance. It's used mainly when doing grid search or selecting models from the AutoML results (`h2o::h2o.automl()`).

description:
## The problem

`collect_metrics` throws an error after tuning with `tune_grid`:  
#> Error: Problem with `mutate()` input `cols`.
#> x `one_of()` must be used within a *selecting* function.
#> ℹ See <https://tidyselect.r-lib.org/reference/faq-selection-context.html>.
#> ℹ Input `cols` is `dplyr::one_of(keep_cols)`.  

I think it's a problem with dplyr v1.0.0 deprecating `group_keys`, which `tune_grid` relies on:
#> Warning: The `...` argument of `group_keys()` is deprecated as of dplyr 1.0.0.
#> Please `group_by()` first
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_warnings()` to see where this warning was generated.

title: tidymodels finalization of tuning parameters
description:
Hi,

This is a cross post from the [RStudio Community Boards](https://community.rstudio.com/t/tidymodels-finalization-of-tuning-parameters/58789)

I am getting the following error when i run the code below

> Error: Some tuning parameters require finalization but there are recipe parameters that require tuning. Please use `parameters()` to finalize the parameter ranges.

``` r
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyverse)

# Create a dataframe where we are trying to predict Setosa
mydf <- iris %>% 
  mutate(set_tgt = factor(ifelse(Species == 'setosa', 'yes', 'no'))) %>% 
  select(-Species)

# Try tune the correlation before removal and the sampling ratio
flower_rec <- recipe(set_tgt ~ ., data = mydf) %>%
  step_downsample(uv_confirmed, under_ratio = tune()) %>% 
  step_corr(recipes::all_numeric(), -recipes::all_outcomes(), threshold = tune())

# Set up the cross validation for this
cv_splits <- vfold_cv(mydf, strata = "set_tgt")

# Create the Random Forest Engine
rf_model <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 5000, min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("ranger")

rf_grid <- grid_regular(
  mtry() %>% range_set(c(1, 20)),
  threshold(),
  under_ratio(),
  min_n() %>% range_set(c(2, 10)),
  levels = 5
)

rf_workflow <- workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(flower_rec) %>% 
  add_model(rf_model)

rf_results <- tune_grid(
  rf_workflow,
  resamples = cv_splits,
  grid = rf_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(roc_auc)
)
#> Error: Some tuning parameters require finalization but there are recipe parameters that require tuning. Please use `parameters()` to finalize the parameter ranges.
```

title: Issues with behind-the-scenes, surprising variable pre-processing and ranger package for random forests
description:
I consistently run into this problem when using the `ranger` package to run a random forest model and I have a feature that is a factor and happens to have spaces in the cell values themselves.

As you can see, the error messages from `fit_resamples()` and `last_fit()` aren't terribly helpful. I'm intentionally using only a formula here, and it seems surprising how difficult this is to get working with anything but a recipe. This is counter-intuitive because I'm explicitly *not* dummifying this variable, but under the hood I believe that `hardhat` is doing this for me. 

For teaching, given these intricacies, I'm using this function instead (also renamed as we are teaching `last_fit()` first):

```
fit_split <- function(formula, model, split, ...) {
  wf <- workflows::add_model(workflows::add_formula(workflows::workflow(), formula, blueprint = hardhat::default_formula_blueprint(indicators = FALSE)), model)
  tune::last_fit(wf, split, ...)
}
```

I have coded a simple `tidymodels` workflow using the Sacramento data from `caret`, and it results in either an odd error or crashes R entirely.

## Reproducible example

```r
# load tidymodels

# create a scaling/centering recipe
sacr_recipe <- recipe(price ~ sqft, data = sacramento_train) %>%

# create a nn model spec
sacr_spec <- nearest_neighbor(weight_func = "rectangular", neighbors = tune()) %>%
```

title: tune engine specific arguments: error on `finalize_workflow`
description:
When tuning Engine-Specific arguments (`max.depth` in this example) `finalize_workflow` throws an error because it does not recognize those argments. Can we only tune main arguments?

``` r
# Example based on: https://www.tidymodels.org/start/tuning/
library(workflows)
library(parsnip)
library(tune)

data(cells, package = "modeldata")

# Define model
tune_spec <- 
  rand_forest(
    trees = tune()       # Main arguments
  ) %>%
  set_engine(
    engine = "ranger",
    max.depth = tune()   # Engine-Specific arguments
  ) %>%
  set_mode("classification")
tune_spec
#> Random Forest Model Specification (classification)
#> 
#> Main Arguments:
#>   trees = tune()
#> 
#> Engine-Specific Arguments:
#>   max.depth = tune()
#> 
#> Computational engine: ranger

# Define grid
tree_grid <- expand.grid(trees = c(5, 10), max.depth = c(7, 9))
tree_grid
#>   trees max.depth
#> 1     5         7
#> 2    10         7
#> 3     5         9
#> 4    10         9

# Create workflow
tree_wf <- 
  workflow() %>%
  add_model(tune_spec) %>%
  add_formula(class ~ .)

# Evaluate parameters
set.seed(234)
tree_res <- 
  tree_wf %>% 
  tune_grid(
    resamples = rsample::vfold_cv(cells),
    grid = tree_grid
  )

# Select best parameters
best_tree <- tree_res %>% select_best("roc_auc")
best_tree
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   trees max.depth .config
#>   <dbl>     <dbl> <fct>  
#> 1    10         7 Model2

# Error finalizing the workflow
final_wf <- 
  tree_wf %>% 
  finalize_workflow(best_tree)
#> Error: Extra arguments will be ignored: `max.depth`
```

title: sample_size and sample_prop in boost_tree
description:
## The problem

I'm having trouble with `sample_size()` and `sample_prop()` on `boost_tree()` model with the `xgboost`engine. 

The `boost_tree()` function takes only a `sample_size` argument. This argument can recieve both number or proportion of data that is exposed to the fitting process.

When setting a proportion range to this parameter (e.g., 0.5 to 0.9), one must use `sample_size = sample_prop(c(0.5, 0.9))`? 

`sample_size = sample_size(c(0.5, 0.9))` returns only ones and zeros to `sample_size` when a grid is made.

I think `sample_size = sample_prop(c(0.5, 0.9))` works, but I've struggled a little to understand. This is not clear in the documentation.

Issues aside, thank you very much for the great package!

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'xts':
#>   method     from
#>   as.zoo.xts zoo
#> ── Attaching packages ────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels 0.1.0 ──
#> ✓ broom     0.5.4     ✓ recipes   0.1.9
#> ✓ dials     0.0.4     ✓ rsample   0.0.5
#> ✓ dplyr     0.8.4     ✓ tibble    2.1.3
#> ✓ ggplot2   3.2.1     ✓ tune      0.0.1
#> ✓ infer     0.5.1     ✓ workflows 0.1.0
#> ✓ parsnip   0.0.5     ✓ yardstick 0.0.5
#> ✓ purrr     0.3.3
#> ── Conflicts ───────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels_conflicts() ──
#> x purrr::discard()  masks scales::discard()
#> x dplyr::filter()   masks stats::filter()
#> x dplyr::lag()      masks stats::lag()
#> x ggplot2::margin() masks dials::margin()
#> x recipes::step()   masks stats::step()

recipe <- recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)

mod_xgboost <- boost_tree(
  mtry = 3,
  trees = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  sample_size = tune()
) %>% 
  set_mode("classification") %>% 
  set_engine("xgboost")

workflow_xgboost <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(recipe) %>%
  add_model(mod_xgboost)

hp_xgboost_size <- workflow_xgboost %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  update(
    sample_size = sample_size(c(0.5, 0.9))
  )

hp_xgboost_prop <- workflow_xgboost %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  update(
    sample_size = sample_prop(c(0.5, 0.9))
  )

grid_size <- grid_regular(hp_xgboost_size, levels = 5)
grid_prop <- grid_regular(hp_xgboost_prop, levels = 5)

unique(grid_size$sample_size)
#> [1] 0

unique(grid_prop$sample_size)
#> [1] 0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9
```

title: mars seems to be quite broken in the current version.  It is even more difficult to understand because it is giving at least 4 different error messages as to what has gone wrong.
description:
Mars use to be working for me about a month ago.  I don't know when it stopped working, I only noticed today, but I guess in the latest version.  

The strange thing is that it gives at least 4 different error messages.  In the reprex below I've managed to reproduce 3 of them, although they are partially cutoff by reprex.  The full messages are :

* Fold01: internal: Error: Must subset elements with a valid subscript vector. Can't convert from double to integer due to loss of precision.
* Fold01: internal: Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE): arguments imply differing number of rows: 7, 8 *{in my own code the 7 has varied from 6 to 1,002, but the 8 has always been 8)}*.
* Fold01: model 1/3: Error: the nfold argument must be specified when pmethod="cv"

title: fit_resamples creates one-hot encoding for some datasets and not for others
description:
## The problem

In light of https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/151, I'm trying to run a resampling of a continuous variable against a character column without one-hot encoding the character column. I took the stackoverflow example from https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/151 and found that it worked. However, once I replicated the exact same thing for `mtcars`, it raises an error.



## Reproducible example

Here's the example using the stackoverflow data:

```r
library(rsample)
library(parsnip)
library(tune)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(modeldata)
data(stackoverflow)

linear_spec <-
  linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  set_mode("regression")


########################## With stackoverflow data ####################
so_split <- initial_split(stackoverflow[c("Salary", "Country")])
so_train <- training(so_split)

# Convert factor to character
so_fold <-
  mutate(so_train, Country = as.character(Country)) %>%
  vfold_cv(v = 10)

# Returns results without errors/warnings
linear_spec %>%
  fit_resamples(
    Salary ~ Country,
    resamples = so_fold 
  )
#> # Resampling results
#> # 10-fold cross-validation 
#> # A tibble: 10 x 4
#>    splits             id     .metrics         .notes          
#>    <list>             <chr>  <list>           <list>          
#>  1 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold01 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  2 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold02 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  3 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold03 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  4 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold04 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  5 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold05 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  6 <split [3.8K/420]> Fold06 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  7 <split [3.8K/419]> Fold07 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  8 <split [3.8K/419]> Fold08 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  9 <split [3.8K/419]> Fold09 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#> 10 <split [3.8K/419]> Fold10 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>

```

This is expected, as character columns are not expanded to dummies. However, if I replace the above with `mtcars`, it raises the typical one-hot encoding problem of not finding variables defined in the formula:

```r
########################## With mtcars data ####################
mt_split <- initial_split(mtcars[c("mpg", "gear")])
mt_train <- as_tibble(training(mt_split))

mt_fold <-
  mt_train %>%
  mutate(gear = as.character(gear)) %>%
  vfold_cv(v = 10)

# Returns results with errors/warnings
linear_spec %>%
  fit_resamples(
    mpg ~ gear,
    resamples = mt_fold 
  )
#> x Fold01: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold03: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold04: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold05: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold06: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold07: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold08: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold09: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> x Fold10: model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Col...
#> Warning: This tuning result has notes. Example notes on model fitting include:
#> model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Column `gear5` doesn't exist.
#> model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Column `gear5` doesn't exist.
#> model (predictions): Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> ✖ Column `gear4` doesn't exist.
#> # Resampling results
#> # 10-fold cross-validation 
#> # A tibble: 10 x 4
#>    splits         id     .metrics         .notes          
#>    <list>         <chr>  <list>           <list>          
#>  1 <split [21/3]> Fold01 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  2 <split [21/3]> Fold02 <tibble [2 × 3]> <tibble [0 × 1]>
#>  3 <split [21/3]> Fold03 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  4 <split [21/3]> Fold04 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  5 <split [22/2]> Fold05 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  6 <split [22/2]> Fold06 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  7 <split [22/2]> Fold07 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  8 <split [22/2]> Fold08 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#>  9 <split [22/2]> Fold09 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
#> 10 <split [22/2]> Fold10 <tibble [0 × 3]> <tibble [1 × 1]>
```

I assume this is not expected, right? Some thoughts:

1. From what I've read in https://github.com/tidymodels/workflows/pull/53, https://github.com/tidymodels/parsnip/pull/332 and https://github.com/tidymodels/hardhat/pull/140, one-hot encoding will only happen with factor columns, in case it is specified in `default_formula_blueprint`. I think this shouldn't happen with character columns, as it's happening now.

2. Surprisingly, the previous error happens in **some** folds but not on all folds.

title: split_to_rset() uses randomness when it doesn't need to
description:
Extracted from https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/11#issuecomment-675648443, because I now believe this is a separate standalone issue.

`split_to_rset()` calls `rsample::mc_cv()` just to get the structure of that rset subclass, but then we override the results with `x`. HOWEVER, it relies on randomness to generate the object that we overwrite. This causes some confusion with reproducibility between `last_fit()` and direct usage of `fit()/predict()`.

```r
> tune:::split_to_rset
function (x) 
{
    prop <- length(x$in_id)/nrow(x$data)
    res <- rsample::mc_cv(x$data, times = 1, prop = prop)
    res$splits[[1]] <- x
    res
}
```

Since we really just need to generate the structure the rset object, we should consider using the below rewrite instead. It is still suboptimal because it hardcodes the structure of an mc_cv rset, but I can live with that.

```r
# Manually construct an `mc_cv()` rset.
# Don't call `mc_cv()` directly, as that will mess with the random seed
split_to_rset <- function(x) {
  times <- 1L
  prop <- length(x$in_id) / nrow(x$data)
  strata <- FALSE
  
  attrib <- list(prop = prop, times = times, strata = strata)
  
  splits <- list(x)
  
  ids <- "Resample1"
  
  rsample::new_rset(
    splits = list(x), 
    ids = ids,
    attrib = attrib,
    subclass = c("mc_cv", "rset")
  )
}
```

title: `tune:::estimate_class()` doesn't respect `yardstick.event_first = FALSE`
description:
Underlying issue of https://github.com/tidymodels/yardstick/issues/166

It seems that `estimate_class()` needs to somehow respect `options(yardstick.event_first = FALSE)` when computing the metric. It looks like it just selects the first `.pred_*()` column currently.

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/fa4dc535e89ad8d039df5ba5717e718485d877f4/R/grid_performance.R#L67-L82

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidymodels)
  library(MLmetrics)
  library(mlbench)
  library(dplyr)
})

# Flip option!
options(yardstick.event_first = FALSE) 

data("PimaIndiansDiabetes2")

set.seed(73487)

# remove duplicates for ranger
data <- PimaIndiansDiabetes2[complete.cases(PimaIndiansDiabetes2),]

xgb_recipe <- recipe(diabetes ~ ., data = data)

xgb_model <- parsnip::rand_forest() %>%
  set_engine("ranger") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

xgb_workflow <- workflows::workflow() %>%
  workflows::add_model(xgb_model) %>%
  workflows::add_recipe(xgb_recipe)

cv_folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(data, strata = diabetes, v = 2)

xgb_fit <- tune::fit_resamples(
  xgb_workflow,
  resamples = cv_folds,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(pr_auc),
  control = tune::control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
)

predictions_resample1 <- xgb_fit$.predictions[[1]]

# The 2nd level is the event!
head(predictions_resample1$diabetes)
#> [1] neg pos pos pos pos pos
#> Levels: neg pos

# So this is how you compute PR AUC
pr_auc(predictions_resample1, diabetes, .pred_pos)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   .metric .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 pr_auc  binary         0.686

# But tune computed it by passing in `.pred_neg`!
xgb_fit$.metrics[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   .metric .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
#> 1 pr_auc  binary         0.205

# i.e. it did this incorrectly
pr_auc(predictions_resample1, diabetes, .pred_neg)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   .metric .estimator .estimate
#>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl>
```

title: XGBoost trains second level, while tidymodels trains first. Is this a problem?
description:
## The problem

I'm concerned with the validity of results from training XGBoost using tidymodels.
tidymodels uses the first level of a factor as the default positive class, while XGBoost defaults to the second (although I couldn't find this in the docs; didn't check source code). Using `options(yardstick.event_first = FALSE)` is not a viable solution, because of https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/240 and https://github.com/tidymodels/yardstick/issues/166, meaning it's possible `select_best()` won't select the best set of parameters based on the PR-AUC.

The problem arises when `butcher::butcher()` the model fit for deployment.
Now, the underlying XGBoost model is predicting the negative model class.
Yes, I can simply `1 - prediction` to get the probability of the positive class, but I'm not sure if that is reliable. 

Was XGBoost in fact trained to predict the negative class? If so, how reliable are the metrics generated by tidymodels and the tuning process and the final predictions?

Also note that, on my actual data with severe class imbalance, the evaluation log from XGBoost has a PR-AUC of 98 on the first boosting iteration, which also tells me it's targeting the wrong class.

Posting here because https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/issues/240, but this may not be a `tune` bug (or an issue at all, for that matter).

## Reproducible example

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidymodels)
  library(MLmetrics)
  library(mlbench)
  library(dplyr)
  library(forcats)
  library(butcher)
})

data("PimaIndiansDiabetes2")

set.seed(73487)

# remove duplicates 
data <- PimaIndiansDiabetes2[complete.cases(PimaIndiansDiabetes2),] %>% 
  # flip levels to avoid issue 240
  mutate(diabetes = forcats::fct_relevel(diabetes, c("pos", "neg")))

xgb_recipe <- recipe(diabetes ~ ., data = data)

xgb_model <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  trees = tune::tune(),
  tree_depth = tune::tune(), min_n = tune::tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune::tune(),
  sample_size = tune::tune(), mtry = tune::tune(),
  learn_rate = tune::tune(),
) %>%
  parsnip::set_engine("xgboost", params = list(eval_metric = "aucpr")) %>%
  parsnip::set_mode(., mode = "classification")

xgb_grid <- dials::grid_max_entropy(
  dials::trees(c(200, 1500)),
  dials::min_n(),
  dials::tree_depth(c(3, 10)),
  dials::loss_reduction(),
  sample_size = dials::sample_prop(c(0.5, 1)),
  dials::finalize(dials::mtry(), recipes::prep(xgb_recipe) %>% recipes::juice()),
  dials::learn_rate(c(0.01, 0.3), trans = NULL),
  size = 10
)

xgb_workflow <- workflows::workflow() %>%
  workflows::add_model(xgb_model) %>%
  workflows::add_recipe(xgb_recipe)

cv_folds <- rsample::vfold_cv(
  data,
  strata = diabetes,
  v = 3
)

xgb_tuned_fit <- tune::tune_grid(
  xgb_workflow,
  resamples = cv_folds,
  grid = xgb_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(pr_auc),
  control = tune::control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
)
```

title: syntax recommender functions
description:
We should have some `suggest()` functions that, given some data information, will print out a scaffold for recipe and model object definitions. 

For example, `suggest_glmnet(Sepal.Length ~ ., data = iris)` might print to the console:

```
rec <-
  recipe(Sepal.Length ~ ., data = iris) %>%
  step_novel(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes(), one_hot = TRUE) %>% 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

mod <- 
  parsnip::linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>% 
  set_mode("regression") %>% 
  set_engine("glmnet")

wflw <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_model(mod) %>% 
  add_recipe(rec)
```

title: Include "composition" in tune_grid()
description:
I don't know if this question is more applicable to the tune package or the workflows package.

Currently, the `bake()` function in recipes allow us to output a `dgCMatrix` using the `composition` argument. 

However, when one works with the workflows package and the tune package we are not able to use that option. I believe currently we are restricted to the tibble. 

Is there any plan to add that option in future releases? 

Thanks! 

Example: 

``` r

# Packages ----------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'xts':
#>   method     from
#>   as.zoo.xts zoo
#> ── Attaching packages ────────────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels 0.0.3 ──
#> ✓ broom     0.5.2          ✓ recipes   0.1.7.9002
#> ✓ dials     0.0.4          ✓ rsample   0.0.5     
#> ✓ infer     0.5.1          ✓ yardstick 0.0.4     
#> ✓ parsnip   0.0.4.9000
#> ── Conflicts ───────────────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels_conflicts() ──
#> x scales::discard()   masks purrr::discard()
#> x dplyr::filter()     masks stats::filter()
#> x recipes::fixed()    masks stringr::fixed()
#> x dplyr::lag()        masks stats::lag()
#> x dials::margin()     masks ggplot2::margin()
#> x yardstick::spec()   masks readr::spec()
#> x recipes::step()     masks stats::step()
#> x recipes::yj_trans() masks scales::yj_trans()
library(textrecipes)
library(workflows)
library(tune)

# Data  --------------------------------------------------------------------

train <- read_csv('train.csv.zip') %>% 
  sample_frac(0.1)
#> Parsed with column specification:
#> cols(
#>   id = col_character(),
#>   comment_text = col_character(),
#>   toxic = col_double(),
#>   severe_toxic = col_double(),
#>   obscene = col_double(),
#>   threat = col_double(),
#>   insult = col_double(),
#>   identity_hate = col_double()
#> )

train <- train %>% 
  mutate(toxic = ifelse(toxic == 1, "yes", "no"))

# Recipe -----------------------------------------------------------------

rec <- recipe(toxic ~ comment_text, data = train) %>% 
  step_tokenize(comment_text) %>% 
  step_stopwords(comment_text) %>% 
  step_tokenfilter(comment_text, max_tokens = 1000) %>% 
  step_tfidf(comment_text)


# Model ------------------------------------------------------------------

model <- logistic_reg(
  mode = "classification",
  penalty = tune(),
  mixture = tune()
) %>% 
  set_engine("glmnet")

# Workflow ---------------------------------------------------------------

toxic_wflow <- workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(rec) %>% 
  add_model(model)

# Grid --------------------------------------------------------------------

param_grid <- grid_regular(
  mixture(),
  penalty(),
  levels = 2
)

# CV ----------------------------------------------------------------------

cv_rs <- vfold_cv(
  train %>% select(toxic, comment_text),
  v = 10,
  strata = toxic
)

# Tune --------------------------------------------------------------------

grid_search <- tune_grid(
  toxic_wflow,
  resamples = cv_rs,
  metrics = metric_set(roc_auc),
  grid = param_grid,

show_best(grid_search, n = 1)
```

title: Custom recipe steps don't work when tuning is done in parallel
description:
## The problem

When a custom recipe step is created, it can be used in a tuning grid when the tuning grid is run sequentially, ie. control_grid(allow_par = FALSE), but not when the tuning grid is run in parallel, ie. allow_par = TRUE.

When run in parallel the following error occurs (in this case I am using the step_percentile example custom step):

* "recipe: Error in UseMethod(\"prep\"): no applicable method for 'prep' applied to an object of class \"c('step_percentile', 'step')\""

## Reproducible example

Below I used the example code from the *recipes* package for creating a custom step, and from the *tune* package for running a model through a tuning grid, with a few modifications that are mostly noted.  You will see at the bottom of the example the "no applicable method for 'prep'" error.  I should also note that I've tried adding step_percentile to a package and adding pkgs="MyPackage" to the control_grid, but this did not make a difference.  

In a second version version of the code, which I've placed underneath, I've modified it to run sequentially and it runs correctly without any issues.

You can skip to the last 20 lines of the example to see the actual relevant code.  Above that is just the definition of the custom step.

### Failing Parallel Version

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> -- Attaching packages ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ tidymodels 0.1.0 --
#> v broom     0.5.5      v recipes   0.1.10
#> v dials     0.0.5      v rsample   0.0.6 
#> v dplyr     0.8.5      v tibble    3.0.0 
#> v ggplot2   3.3.0      v tune      0.0.1 
#> v infer     0.5.1      v workflows 0.1.1 
#> v parsnip   0.0.5      v yardstick 0.0.6 
#> v purrr     0.3.3
#> -- Conflicts --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- tidymodels_conflicts() --
#> x purrr::discard()  masks scales::discard()
#> x dplyr::filter()   masks stats::filter()
#> x dplyr::lag()      masks stats::lag()
#> x ggplot2::margin() masks dials::margin()
#> x recipes::step()   masks stats::step()
library(mlbench)
library(doParallel)
#> Loading required package: foreach
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'foreach'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:purrr':
#> 
#>     accumulate, when
#> Loading required package: iterators
#> Loading required package: parallel

### RECIPES

step_percentile <- function(
  recipe, ..., 
  role = NA, 
  trained = FALSE, 
  ref_dist = NULL,
  approx = FALSE, 
  options = list(probs = (0:100)/100, names = TRUE),
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("percentile")
) {
  
  ## The variable selectors are not immediately evaluated by using
  ##  the `quos` function in `rlang`. `ellipse_check` captures the
  ##  values and also checks to make sure that they are not empty.  
  terms <- recipes::ellipse_check(...) 
  
  recipes::add_step(
    recipe, 
    step_percentile_new(
      terms = terms, 
      trained = trained,
      role = role, 
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  )
}

step_percentile_new <- 
  function(terms, role, trained, ref_dist, approx, options, skip, id) {
    step(
      subclass = "percentile", 
      terms = terms,
      role = role,
      trained = trained,
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  }

get_pctl <- function(x, args) {
  args$x <- x
  do.call("quantile", args)
}

prep.step_percentile <- function(x, training, info = NULL, ...) {
  col_names <- recipes::terms_select(terms = x$terms, info = info) 
  ## You can add error trapping for non-numeric data here and so on. See the
  ## `check_type` function to do this for basic types. 
  
  ## We'll use the names later so
  if (x$options$names == FALSE)
    rlang::abort("`names` should be set to TRUE")
  
  if (!x$approx) {
    ref_dist <- training[, col_names]
  } else {
    ref_dist <- purrr::map(training[, col_names],  get_pctl, args = x$options)
  }
  
  ## Use the constructor function to return the updated object. 
  ## Note that `trained` is set to TRUE
  
  step_percentile_new(
    terms = x$terms, 
    trained = TRUE,
    role = x$role, 
    ref_dist = ref_dist,
    approx = x$approx,
    options = x$options,
    skip = x$skip,
    id = x$id
  )
}

## Two helper functions
pctl_by_mean <- function(x, ref) mean(ref <= x)

pctl_by_approx <- function(x, ref) {
  ## go from 1 column tibble to vector
  x <- getElement(x, names(x))
  ## get the percentiles values from the names (e.g. "10%")
  p_grid <- as.numeric(gsub("%$", "", names(ref))) 
  approx(x = ref, y = p_grid, xout = x)$y/100
}

bake.step_percentile <- function(object, new_data, ...) {
  require(tibble)
  ## For illustration (and not speed), we will loop through the affected variables
  ## and do the computations
  vars <- names(object$ref_dist)
  
  for (i in vars) {
    if (!object$approx) {
      ## We can use `apply` since tibbles do not drop dimensions:
      new_data[, i] <- apply(new_data[, i], 1, pctl_by_mean, 
                             ref = object$ref_dist[, i])
    } else 
      new_data[, i] <- pctl_by_approx(new_data[, i], object$ref_dist[[i]])
  }
  ## Always convert to tibbles on the way out
  as_tibble(new_data)
}


### TUNE
data(Ionosphere)

Ionosphere <- Ionosphere %>% select(-V2)

svm_mod <-
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

iono_rec <-
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = Ionosphere)  %>%
  # In case V1 is has a single value sampled
  step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) %>% 
  # convert it to a dummy variable
  step_dummy(V1) %>%
  # Scale it the same as the others
  step_range(matches("V1_")) %>% 
  step_percentile(recipes::all_numeric()) # custom step added to the recipe

set.seed(4943)
iono_rs <- bootstraps(Ionosphere, times = 5) # times reduced to speed up sequential model tuning

roc_vals <- metric_set(roc_auc)

cluster = makeCluster(detectCores()) # Create a cluster
registerDoParallel(cluster)

ctrl <- control_grid(verbose = FALSE, allow_par = TRUE) # Run in parallel

set.seed(35)
grid_form <-
  tune_grid(
    iono_rec,
    model = svm_mod,
    resamples = iono_rs,
    metrics = roc_vals,
    control = ctrl
  )
#> Warning: All models failed in tune_grid(). See the `.notes` column.
print(grid_form$.notes[[1]])
#> # A tibble: 1 x 1
#>   .notes                                                                        
#>   <chr>                                                                         
#> 1 "recipe: Error in UseMethod(\"prep\"): no applicable method for 'prep' applie~
```

``` r
library(mlbench)

### RECIPES

step_percentile <- function(
  recipe, ..., 
  role = NA, 
  trained = FALSE, 
  ref_dist = NULL,
  approx = FALSE, 
  options = list(probs = (0:100)/100, names = TRUE),
  skip = FALSE,
  id = rand_id("percentile")
) {
  
  ## The variable selectors are not immediately evaluated by using
  ##  the `quos` function in `rlang`. `ellipse_check` captures the
  ##  values and also checks to make sure that they are not empty.  
  terms <- recipes::ellipse_check(...) 
  
  recipes::add_step(
    recipe, 
    step_percentile_new(
      terms = terms, 
      trained = trained,
      role = role, 
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  )
}

step_percentile_new <- 
  function(terms, role, trained, ref_dist, approx, options, skip, id) {
    step(
      subclass = "percentile", 
      terms = terms,
      role = role,
      trained = trained,
      ref_dist = ref_dist,
      approx = approx,
      options = options,
      skip = skip,
      id = id
    )
  }

get_pctl <- function(x, args) {
  args$x <- x
  do.call("quantile", args)
}

prep.step_percentile <- function(x, training, info = NULL, ...) {
  col_names <- recipes::terms_select(terms = x$terms, info = info) 
  ## You can add error trapping for non-numeric data here and so on. See the
  ## `check_type` function to do this for basic types. 
  
  ## We'll use the names later so
  if (x$options$names == FALSE)
    rlang::abort("`names` should be set to TRUE")
  
  if (!x$approx) {
    ref_dist <- training[, col_names]
  } else {
    ref_dist <- purrr::map(training[, col_names],  get_pctl, args = x$options)
  }
  
  ## Use the constructor function to return the updated object. 
  ## Note that `trained` is set to TRUE
  
  step_percentile_new(
    terms = x$terms, 
    trained = TRUE,
    role = x$role, 
    ref_dist = ref_dist,
    approx = x$approx,
    options = x$options,
    skip = x$skip,
    id = x$id
  )
}

## Two helper functions
pctl_by_mean <- function(x, ref) mean(ref <= x)

pctl_by_approx <- function(x, ref) {
  ## go from 1 column tibble to vector
  x <- getElement(x, names(x))
  ## get the percentiles values from the names (e.g. "10%")
  p_grid <- as.numeric(gsub("%$", "", names(ref))) 
  approx(x = ref, y = p_grid, xout = x)$y/100
}

bake.step_percentile <- function(object, new_data, ...) {
  require(tibble)
  ## For illustration (and not speed), we will loop through the affected variables
  ## and do the computations
  vars <- names(object$ref_dist)
  
  for (i in vars) {
    if (!object$approx) {
      ## We can use `apply` since tibbles do not drop dimensions:
      new_data[, i] <- apply(new_data[, i], 1, pctl_by_mean, 
                             ref = object$ref_dist[, i])
    } else 
      new_data[, i] <- pctl_by_approx(new_data[, i], object$ref_dist[[i]])
  }
  ## Always convert to tibbles on the way out
  as_tibble(new_data)
}
```

title: grid code paths for cubist models (and maybe others)
description:
Although the `cubist_rules` model specification has a multi_predict generic function for neighbors, the 'tune' package does not recognize it because the grid path is not set. So currently Cubist retrains when tuning neighbors.

From examing tune, I could temporarily resolve this within my own scripts by using the `fit_max_value` path:

```
min_grid.cubist_rules <- tune:::fit_max_value
```

Not sure if this should go into tune or rules. I guess in due course it would be good to have some documentation on how to specify min_grid methods if users are creating their own model specifications.

title: finalize_workflow() assigns incorrect values when finalizing multiple recipes steps of the same type
description:
## The problem

Hi,

Thanks for a great package, I really appreciate all the work that y'all have put into this and the other tidymodels packages!

I believe I've found a bug in finalize_workflow() that gives incorrect values when finalizing multiple recipes steps of the same type. I ran into this when tuning the polynomial degree for several vars using step_poly(). Here's a minimal reprex.

## Reproducible example

Sorry, couldn't get reprex::reprex() to work, but this code should run. 

```r
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(recipes)
library(parsnip)
library(dials)
library(tune)
library(workflows)

lm_rec <- 
  recipe(form = mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) %>% 
  step_poly(drat, degree = tune("drat_deg")) %>% 
  step_poly(disp, degree = tune("disp_deg")) %>% 
  step_poly(hp, degree = tune("hp_deg"))

lm_spec <- linear_reg(penalty = 0, mixture = 0) %>% set_engine("lm")

lm_wf <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(lm_rec) %>% 
  add_model(lm_spec)

lm_grid <- 
  parameters(lm_rec) %>% 
  grid_regular() %>% 
  slice(8)

lm_grid

# Gives incorrect output
lm_wf %>% 
  finalize_workflow(lm_grid) %>% 
  pull_workflow_preprocessor() %>% 
  prep(mtcars) %>% 
  bake(new_data = mtcars) %>% 
  glimpse()

# This works though
lm_rec %>% 
  merge(lm_grid) %>% 
  .$x %>% 
  pluck(1) %>% 
  prep(mtcars) %>% 
  bake(new_data = mtcars) %>% 
  glimpse()
```
Here's a screenshot of the output - finalize_workflow() results in 3 poly terms for drat (instead of two) and 2 poly terms for disp (instead of 3). The when I merge the grid object into the recipe is correct, however. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2652489/97762771-3e420a80-1acf-11eb-8a26-06ff648eb57a.png)

I believe that the params are being applied in the sorted order of the recipe step names, rather than by matching on the name of the parameter.

title: last_fit() and fit() give different probability predictions for the same workflow and data
description:
When the same workflow is used with last_fit() and fit() on the same training and testing data, the probability predictions are different. Below is a reproducible example where I fit the same workflow 4 times using an identical seed. Twice with last_fit() and twice with fit(). The 2 probability predictions of last_fit() are identical to each other and the 2 probability predictions of fit() are identical to each other, however the probability predictions of last_fit() and fit() are very different (not a rounding problem).

Note that this problem happens whether or not parallel processing is used - using the below line for example:
```r
# doParallel::registerDoParallel(cores = 7)
```
## Reproducible example

```r
library(tidyverse)
suppressMessages(library(tidymodels))
library(modeldata)
suppressMessages(library(themis))
library(embed)
data(attrition)

attrition <- janitor::clean_names(attrition)

attrition <- attrition %>% 
  mutate(attrition_class = fct_rev(attrition)) %>% 
  select(-attrition)

levels(attrition$attrition_class)
#> [1] "Yes" "No"

set.seed(1954)
attrition_split <- initial_split(attrition, strata = "attrition_class")
attrition_train <- training(attrition_split)
attrition_test <- testing(attrition_split)

xgboost_recipe <- 
  recipe(formula = attrition_class ~ ., data = attrition_train) %>% 
  step_upsample(attrition_class, seed = 936) %>% 
  step_discretize_xgb(age, daily_rate, distance_from_home, hourly_rate,
                      monthly_income, monthly_rate, total_working_years,
                      years_at_company, outcome = "attrition_class") %>% 
  step_novel(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes()) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes(), one_hot = TRUE) %>% 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) 

xgboost_spec <- 
  boost_tree(trees = 462, min_n = 9, tree_depth = 15, learn_rate = 0.02160385, 
             loss_reduction = 0.6299069, sample_size = 0.1487263) %>% 
  set_mode("classification") %>% 
  set_engine("xgboost") 

xgboost_workflow <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(xgboost_recipe) %>% 
  add_model(xgboost_spec)

common_seed <- 12345

# fit 2 models by last fit and 2 models by fit using the same seed
set.seed(common_seed)
last_fit1 <- last_fit(xgboost_workflow, attrition_split)

set.seed(common_seed)
last_fit2 <- last_fit(xgboost_workflow, attrition_split)

set.seed(common_seed)
fit1 <- fit(xgboost_workflow, attrition_train)

set.seed(common_seed)
fit2 <- fit(xgboost_workflow, attrition_train)

# get predictions of all 4 models
last_fit1_pred <- last_fit1[[5]][[1]]
last_fit2_pred <- last_fit2[[5]][[1]]

fit1_pred <- predict(fit1, attrition_test, type = "prob")

fit2_pred <- predict(fit2, attrition_test, type = "prob")

# see predictions of all 4 models
head(last_fit1_pred)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   .pred_Yes .pred_No  .row .pred_class attrition_class
#>       <dbl>    <dbl> <int> <fct>       <fct>          
#> 1     0.243    0.757    13 No          No             
#> 2     0.255    0.745    16 No          No             
#> 3     0.366    0.634    22 No          Yes            
#> 4     0.788    0.212    27 Yes         Yes            
#> 5     0.237    0.763    28 No          No             
#> 6     0.239    0.761    41 No          No

head(last_fit2_pred)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   .pred_Yes .pred_No  .row .pred_class attrition_class
#>       <dbl>    <dbl> <int> <fct>       <fct>          
#> 1     0.243    0.757    13 No          No             
#> 2     0.255    0.745    16 No          No             
#> 3     0.366    0.634    22 No          Yes            
#> 4     0.788    0.212    27 Yes         Yes            
#> 5     0.237    0.763    28 No          No             
#> 6     0.239    0.761    41 No          No

head(fit1_pred)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 2
#>   .pred_Yes .pred_No
#>       <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     0.351    0.649
#> 2     0.231    0.769
#> 3     0.324    0.676
#> 4     0.865    0.135
#> 5     0.158    0.842
#> 6     0.217    0.783

head(fit2_pred)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 2
#>   .pred_Yes .pred_No
#>       <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     0.351    0.649
#> 2     0.231    0.769
#> 3     0.324    0.676
#> 4     0.865    0.135
#> 5     0.158    0.842
#> 6     0.217    0.783

# last_fit prediction probabilities identical to each other
identical(last_fit1_pred$.pred_Yes, last_fit2_pred$.pred_Yes)
#> [1] TRUE

# fit prediction probabilities identical to each other
identical(fit1_pred$.pred_Yes, fit2_pred$.pred_Yes)
#> [1] TRUE

# last_fit prediction probabilities NOT identical to fit prediction probabilities
identical(last_fit1_pred$.pred_Yes, fit1_pred$.pred_Yes)
#> [1] FALSE
```

title: Sparsity for tuning
description:
Currently the tuning step does not seem to support sparsity, as the rsample package need
a data frame as input:

```
#defne training test split
train_test_split <-
  rsample::initial_split(
    data = fingerprintsAll,     
    prop = 0.80   
  ) 

And for instance the tune bayes needs an resample object: 
xgb_search <- tune_bayes(xgb_workflow, 
                         resamples = ames_vfold,
                         initial = 25, iter = 50,
                         param_info = xgb_param,
                         control = ctrl)
```
There are functions like juice() and bake() that can export dgcMatrix so it seems to be supported
somehow. Is it possible to specify somewhere that a data frame is transformed to a dgcMatrix
before passing it into the model (i.e. xgboost). Maybe in the recipe or workflow packages. ?

title: optimize iterators
description:
In cases where there are a lot of workers and a fast pre-processor, collapse the `for` loops and parallel process over all combinations. Also, if there is a single resample, we should iterate over the parameters. 

`tune_grid()` should be able to have good heuristics on what the best approach would be _given the tuning grid_. In the future, we should have more workflows and have `quarterback()` be able to more dynamically determine the appropriate items to iterate over.

title: How to attain maximum CPU utilisation in Parallel Processing
description:
Hi
I am trying to utilize the maximum cores available for tuning my grid. However, even after registering all the cores (either by DoParallel or DoFuture) it only uses cores equivalent to the resampling loop of grid search. Is this by design or is there a way to expand the run to all cores and improve efficiency?

Thanks

title: Cannot get tune_bayes() work in parallel on doRedis
description:
Regarding [this issue](https://github.com/bwlewis/doRedis/issues/57), I created an example to reproduce it. I was expecting the script to be blocked because no Redis worker was created, however, it just ran like `doRedis` was not registered.

```r
library(tidymodels)
library(modeldata)

data(cells)

set.seed(2369)
tr_te_split <- initial_split(cells %>% select(-case), prop = 3/4)
cell_train <- training(tr_te_split)
cell_test  <- testing(tr_te_split)

set.seed(1697)
folds <- vfold_cv(cell_train, v = 10)

library(themis)

cell_pre_proc <-
    recipe(class ~ ., data = cell_train) %>%
    step_YeoJohnson(all_predictors()) %>%
    step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>%
    step_pca(all_predictors(), num_comp = tune()) %>%
    step_downsample(class)

svm_mod <-
    svm_rbf(mode = "classification", cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
    set_engine("kernlab")

svm_wflow <-
    workflow() %>%
    add_model(svm_mod) %>%
    add_recipe(cell_pre_proc)

svm_set <- parameters(svm_wflow)

svm_set <-
    svm_set %>%
    update(num_comp = num_comp(c(0L, 20L)))
set.seed(12)

library(doRedis)
registerDoRedis("debug_jobs") # No Redis worker is created.

search_res <-
    svm_wflow %>%
    tune_bayes(
        resamples = folds,
        param_info = svm_set,
        initial = 5,
        iter = 10,
        metrics = metric_set(roc_auc),
        control = control_bayes(no_improve = 5, verbose = TRUE)
    )

removeQueue("debug_jobs")

```

title: Parallel-safe RNG
description:
Hi, I think you want to use `doRNG::%dorng%` instead of just `%dopar%` to make sure you use the L'Ecuyer RNG in order to get statistically sound random numbers for the parallel processing.

You can detect this by running:

```r
library(doFuture)
registerDoFuture()
plan(multicore)  ## same as doMC()
example("tune_grid", package="tune")
```

which warns about this:

```r
> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: UNRELIABLE VALUE: Future ('doFuture-1') unexpectedly generated random numbers without specifying argument
'[future.]seed'. There is a risk that those random numbers are not statistically sound and the overall results
might be invalid. To fix this, specify argument '[future.]seed', e.g. 'seed=TRUE'. This ensures that proper, 
parallel-safe random numbers are produced via the L'Ecuyer-CMRG method. To disable this check,
use [future].seed=NULL, or set option 'future.rng.onMisuse' to "ignore".
...
```

When using `%dorng%`, the **doRNG** package will set up the L'Ecuyer RNG for you and these warnings go away.


PS. I'm working on making those RNG warnings more informative when using **foreach**, e.g. to have them refer to `doRNG::%dorng%` rather than the non-existing 'seed' argument

title: enable tuning functions to have access to model-based statistcs
description:
For example, if someone want to tune a random forest or other tree-based model to maximize accuracy but with a minimal number of predictors. 

I'm not sure if we could/should do this via the `extracts` or a `yardstick` metric set. 

Currently, for grid search, this can be done by using `collect_metrics()` and merging it with the extracts. For sequential search, we can't do it just yet. 

This issue is somewhat related to tidymodels/yardstick#177

title: Submodels don't validate parameter ranges
description:
Consider what happens when you try and tune a model with a grid containing `penalty = -1` vs one containing `penalty = c(-1, 1)` where `-1` is seen as a submodel of `1`.

For the first, we get nice error messages. For the second, we don't get any error messages, and predictions are made for the `penalty = -1` case.

This might be somewhat hard to fix, since these checks on `penalty` happen when you actually run the model through parsnip, but the model with `penalty = -1` is never actually run.

``` r
library(tidymodels)
library(tune)

set.seed(7898)
data_folds <- vfold_cv(mtcars, v = 2)

rec <- recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) %>%
  step_bs(disp, deg_free = tune())

model <- linear_reg(mode = "regression", penalty = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")



cars_grid_1 <- tibble(deg_free = 10L, penalty = -1)

cars_res_1 <- tune_grid(
  rec, 
  model = model,
  resamples = data_folds, 
  grid = cars_grid_1, 
  control = control_grid(extract = function(x) {1}, save_pred = TRUE)
)
#> x Fold1: recipe 1/1, model 1/1: Error: The amount of regularization should be >= 0
#> x Fold2: recipe 1/1, model 1/1: Error: The amount of regularization should be >= 0
#> Warning: All models failed in tune_grid(). See the `.notes` column.

cars_res_1
#> #  2-fold cross-validation 
#> # A tibble: 2 x 6
#>   splits          id    .metrics .notes           .extracts .predictions
#> * <list>          <chr> <list>   <list>           <list>    <list>      
#> 1 <split [16/16]> Fold1 <NULL>   <tibble [1 × 1]> <NULL>    <NULL>      
#> 2 <split [16/16]> Fold2 <NULL>   <tibble [1 × 1]> <NULL>    <NULL>

# -1 is a submodel of 1
cars_grid_2 <- tibble(deg_free = 10L, penalty = c(-1, 1))

cars_res_2 <- tune_grid(
  rec, 
  model = model,
  resamples = data_folds, 
  grid = cars_grid_2, 
  control = control_grid(extract = function(x) {1}, save_pred = TRUE)
)
#> ! Fold2: recipe 1/1, model 1/1 (predictions): some 'x' values beyond boundary knots may cause ill-conditioned bases

cars_res_2
#> #  2-fold cross-validation 
#> # A tibble: 2 x 6
#>   splits       id    .metrics      .notes          .extracts .predictions  
#> * <list>       <chr> <list>        <list>       <list<df[,3> <list>        
#> 1 <split [16/… Fold1 <tibble [4 ×… <tibble [0 …      [1 × 3] <tibble [32 ×…
#> 2 <split [16/… Fold2 <tibble [4 ×… <tibble [1 …      [1 × 3] <tibble [32 ×…
```

title: glmnet for fixed penalty
description: Since `parsnip` wants to fit the whole path (and ignores the given single penalty value), we need to find an approach for using `linear_reg(penalty = 10^-5, mixture = tune())` or similar. Maybe a custom `update()` method for `glmnet` models?
